def: A lease granted by an existing tenant to a third party for part or all of the leased property.
ex: The café operated under a sublease from the restaurant chain that held the head lease.

def: Capable of being transferred to another owner.
ex: The court held that the lease was freely alienable because it contained no covenant against assignment.

def: A person who owns land or a building outright for an unlimited period.
ex: The freeholder refused consent for the flat owners to install a roof terrace.

def: A person who holds property under a lease for a fixed term.
ex: Leaseholders in the block challenged the service charge at the tribunal.

def: To burden property with a charge, claim or restriction.
ex: The farm was heavily encumbered with mortgages taken out over several decades.

def: Not capable of being annulled, lost or made void.
ex: Registration was meant to give the purchaser an indefeasible title to the parcel.

def: The principle that a registered title cannot be defeated by earlier unregistered claims.
ex: The appeal turned on whether indefeasibility protected a buyer who had acquired title through a forged transfer.

def: Acquired through long, uninterrupted use rather than by express grant.
ex: The neighbours claimed a prescriptive right of way after twenty-five years of driving across the field.

def: The act of depriving someone of land or property they occupy.
ex: The squatter had to prove dispossession of the paper owner for the full statutory period.

def: To deprive someone of the land or property they hold.
ex: The bank sought an order to dispossess the borrowers after months of unpaid instalments.

def: To share a common boundary with another piece of land.
ex: The development site abuts a conservation area on its northern edge.

def: A boundary of land described by reference to the properties that adjoin it.
ex: The old conveyance identified the plot only by its abuttals to the church and the mill.

def: The fixing or marking of a boundary or limit.
ex: A surveyor was instructed to resolve the demarcation of the disputed hedge line.

def: To intrude gradually beyond a boundary onto another's land.
ex: The new extension encroached thirty centimetres onto the neighbour's garden.

def: A person who holds property jointly or in common with others.
ex: One cotenant cannot exclude the others from any part of the shared house.

def: The holding of property by two or more people at the same time.
ex: The cotenancy ended when the siblings agreed to sell the cottage and split the proceeds.

def: Relating to the terms or system under which land is held.
ex: The historian traced how tenurial obligations shaped the village's medieval layout.

def: A formal release of any interest a person may have in a property, without warranty of title.
ex: The former partner signed a quitclaim so the house could be sold free of his claim.

def: Relating to an official register recording the extent, value and ownership of land.
ex: The government digitised its cadastral maps to speed up property transactions.

def: An official public register of land parcels, boundaries and ownership.
ex: Errors in the national cadastre left hundreds of rural plots without a clear owner.

def: A change in the permitted use of land under planning regulations.
ex: The rezoning of the industrial estate for housing sent land values soaring.

def: To take private property for public use, usually by state authority.
ex: The ministry moved to expropriate farmland along the planned rail corridor.

def: Fit and in suitable condition to be occupied by a tenant.
ex: The lease required the landlord to keep the premises in good and tenantable repair.

def: The condition of being fit and safe to live in.
ex: Persistent damp and mould led the tribunal to question the flat's habitability.

def: Toleration of continued occupation without the owner's express consent.
ex: After the lease expired, the tenant remained in the shop merely at sufferance.

def: The person to whom property is sold.
ex: The vendee paid the deposit on exchange and took possession at completion.

def: Situated directly beneath, especially of land providing support to the surface above.
ex: Mining under the village withdrew the subjacent support and caused the cottages to subside.

def: The state or right of owning property.
ex: The register showed a change in proprietorship following the death of the sole owner.

def: To take possession of mortgaged property because the borrower has defaulted.
ex: The lender threatened to foreclose unless the arrears were cleared within thirty days.

def: A person who holds property under a sublease from an existing tenant.
ex: The sublessee was bound by the user covenants contained in the head lease.

def: A tenant who grants a sublease of the property they hold.
ex: As sublessor, the agency remained liable to the freeholder for the full rent.

def: A person who holds land from a tenant rather than directly from the owner.
ex: When the head lease was forfeited, the undertenant applied for relief to protect its occupation.

def: A person holding property under an underlease granted by a tenant.
ex: The underlessee could not assign without the consent of both its landlord and the superior landlord.

def: The attaching of a benefit or object to land so that it passes with the land.
ex: Express annexation in the 1920s conveyance meant the restrictive covenant benefited every later owner.

def: To set or mark the boundaries of an area.
ex: Stone posts were installed to demarcate the extent of the right of way.

def: A public path over which people may ride or lead horses as well as walk.
ex: The landowner was ordered to remove the gate obstructing the bridleway.

def: Intermediate in rank or time, especially of a landlord between the owner and the occupier.
ex: The mesne landlord was caught between demands from the freeholder and complaints from the occupiers.

def: A piece of land owned or leased, or the act of holding land.
ex: The duke's landholdings stretched across three counties.

def: A small agricultural holding, often let to a tenant farmer.
ex: The council sold off its remaining smallholdings to raise capital.

def: A small fixed rent paid by a tenant in lieu of feudal services.
ex: Older title deeds still referred to a quitrent payable to the lord of the manor.

def: Land attached to a parish church and providing income for the clergy.
ex: The diocese applied to sell part of the glebe for a small housing scheme.

def: Relating to a manor or to the rights attached to its lordship.
ex: Homeowners were surprised to find manorial rights over minerals registered against their titles.

def: The ground beneath the surface, which ordinarily belongs to the landowner.
ex: The highway authority owned the road surface while the frontagers retained the subsoil.

def: Suitable or available to be rented out.
ex: The refurbishment added four thousand square feet of lettable office space.

def: A tenancy granted by an existing tenant out of their own interest.
ex: The landlord argued that the unauthorised subtenancy breached the lease.

def: A person who rents property from a tenant rather than from the owner.
ex: The subtenant had no direct contract with the freeholder.

def: The grant by a tenant of a lesser lease of the premises they hold.
ex: The alienation clause prohibited underletting of part of the premises.

def: A person to whom property is transferred.
ex: The alienee took the land subject to all the restrictive covenants on the title.

def: A person who transfers property to another.
ex: The alienor warranted that the estate was free from undisclosed charges.

def: The quality of being incapable of transfer to another owner.
ex: The inalienability of the National Trust's land protects it from compulsory sale.

def: Free from any charge, claim or restriction.
ex: The buyer insisted on receiving an unencumbered title at completion.

def: The person who holds legal title to a property.
ex: Only the registered titleholder could grant the easement over the driveway.

def: To accept a higher offer on a property after already agreeing a sale with another buyer.
ex: The couple were gazumped a week before exchange when another bidder offered ten thousand more.

def: To lower an agreed offer on a property just before contracts are exchanged.
ex: The buyer gazundered the seller by demanding a price cut on the eve of exchange.

def: A person who shares an inherited estate equally with other heirs.
ex: The three daughters held the manor as coparceners after their father died without a son.

def: The continued occupation of premises by a tenant after the lease has ended.
ex: The landlord claimed double rent for the tenant's overholding.

def: Describing alterations by a tenant that improve rather than damage the land.
ex: The court treated the barn conversion as ameliorative waste and refused an injunction.

def: An improvement made to land or property that increases its value.
ex: The tenant sought compensation for meliorations made to the farmhouse during the lease.

def: An arrangement in which an owner sells property and then leases it back from the buyer.
ex: The retailer raised capital through a leaseback of its flagship store.

def: The principal lease granted directly by the freeholder, out of which subleases are created.
ex: Every underlease in the shopping centre had to be consistent with the headlease.

def: Existing since a time beyond legal memory or record.
ex: The villagers asserted an immemorial custom to dry their nets on the green.

def: The company or person that buys control of another company in a takeover.
ex: The acquiror insisted on a break fee to protect itself against a rival bid.

def: The company whose control is obtained by another in an acquisition.
ex: The acquiree's pension deficit was ring-fenced in a separate indemnity.

def: A shareholder who votes against or formally objects to a corporate transaction.
ex: The scheme allows dissenters to apply to the court within twenty-one days of the vote.

def: The court-approved imposition of a restructuring plan on dissenting classes of creditors or shareholders.
ex: The company relied on a cross-class cramdown to bind the hold-out bondholders.

def: Complete agreement among all members, often required for certain reserved corporate decisions.
ex: The joint venture agreement demanded unanimity for any change to the business plan.

def: A person who signs and files the documents that legally create a company.
ex: The incorporator resigned once the first directors had been appointed.

def: The position or term of office of a company director.
ex: She held three non-executive directorships alongside her role at the bank.

def: The act of a company creating and offering new shares or debt securities.
ex: The issuance of new preference shares required a special resolution.

def: A bank that guarantees to buy any unsold securities in an offering, taking on the placement risk.
ex: The underwriters agreed to take up any shares left unsubscribed in the rights issue.

def: A corporation formed of several unrelated businesses under common ownership.
ex: Investors pushed the conglomerate to break itself up into focused listed companies.

def: An Irish court-protection procedure in which an examiner tries to rescue an insolvent company.
ex: Examinership gave the airline a hundred days of protection from its creditors.

def: An investor who owns bonds issued by a company and is therefore one of its creditors.
ex: Bondholders rejected the exchange offer and threatened to accelerate the debt.

def: An investor who holds notes, a form of debt security, issued by a company.
ex: A majority of noteholders consented to waive the change-of-control covenant.

def: An accumulated amount of unpaid dividends or debt that is overdue.
ex: Preferred holders must receive the full arrearage before any ordinary dividend is paid.

def: The final date by which conditions must be satisfied, failing which either party may terminate the deal.
ex: With antitrust clearance delayed, the parties agreed to extend the longstop by three months.

def: To close a deal knowing of a breach of warranty and then claim for it afterwards.
ex: The seller added an anti-sandbagging clause so the buyer could not sandbag after completion.

def: To make a higher offer than a rival bidder for the same company.
ex: The private equity house overbid the strategic buyer by fifty pence a share.

def: The conversion of a member-owned mutual organisation into a company owned by shareholders.
ex: Members received free shares on the building society's demutualisation.

def: Describing directorships or shareholdings where the same people or companies sit on or own each other's boards.
ex: Regulators questioned the interlocking directorships between the two competitors.

def: The number or proportion of shares in a company owned by a person or entity.
ex: Once its shareholding passed thirty per cent, the fund was obliged to make a mandatory offer.

def: An issue of new shares sold directly to selected institutional investors rather than to the public.
ex: The company raised forty million pounds through an accelerated placing overnight.

def: Describing share capital that shareholders have agreed to pay but which the company has not yet demanded.
ex: The liquidator called up the uncalled capital to pay the company's creditors.

def: Describing a security that the issuer may redeem before maturity at a set price.
ex: The callable preference shares allowed the issuer to refinance once rates fell.

def: Describing shares that carry economic rights but no right to vote at general meetings.
ex: The founders kept control by issuing only nonvoting shares to outside investors.

def: The position of chair of a board or committee, or the period during which it is held.
ex: Under her chairmanship the board split the roles of chair and chief executive.

def: A shareholder who formally demands that directors call a general meeting.
ex: The requisitionists proposed resolutions to remove two directors.

def: An institution that holds underlying shares and issues receipts representing them to investors.
ex: The depositary issued receipts so foreign investors could trade the shares locally.

def: The removal of a company or security from an official register.
ex: After the takeover, the acquiror applied for deregistration of the target's shares.

def: The diversion of a company's assets or profits to its controlling shareholders at minority investors' expense.
ex: Minority investors alleged tunnelling through related-party sales at below-market prices.

def: The extra value or cost savings expected from combining two businesses.
ex: The bidder justified the premium with two hundred million pounds of annual synergy.

def: Occurring or required before a merger is completed.
ex: The deal stalled while the parties waited for premerger clearance from the competition authority.

def: A transaction in which controlling shareholders force out minority holders, usually for cash.
ex: The court scrutinised the freezeout for fair dealing and fair price.

def: The degree to which shares or rights may be sold or assigned to another party.
ex: The articles restricted the transferability of shares to approved family members.

def: The quality of securities being interchangeable with others of the same class.
ex: The new shares will rank equally to preserve fungibility with the existing listed class.

def: A person who gives property, such as shares, as security for a debt.
ex: The pledgor retained voting rights until an event of default occurred.

def: The party in whose favour property is pledged as security.
ex: On default the pledgee was entitled to sell the shares without a court order.

def: The reuse by a lender or broker of collateral pledged to it as security for its own borrowing.
ex: The prime brokerage agreement capped rehypothecation at the client's outstanding debit balance.

def: To secure a loan or obligation by pledging specific assets.
ex: The fund collateralised the acquisition loan with its shares in the target.

def: The completion of the steps, such as registration, that make a security interest effective against third parties.
ex: Failure to register within twenty-one days prevented perfection of the charge.

def: Governing the relative rights and priorities of different classes of a borrower's creditors.
ex: The intercreditor agreement barred the mezzanine lenders from enforcing during the standstill.

def: To rank a debt or claim below others in priority of payment.
ex: The shareholder agreed to subordinate its loans to the senior bank debt.

def: To remove someone from a position, such as a directorship, by force or vote.
ex: Shareholders voted to oust the entire board at the extraordinary meeting.

def: The system of rules, practices and controls by which a company is directed and held accountable.
ex: Weak governance allowed the founder to approve his own related-party deals.

def: The practice of a director holding too many board seats to perform each role properly.
ex: Proxy advisers recommended voting against him on grounds of overboarding.

def: To appoint someone to a board by vote of the existing members rather than by shareholders.
ex: The directors co-opted an interim member until the next annual general meeting.

def: Describing share awards or options that the holder is not yet entitled to keep or exercise.
ex: On a change of control, all unvested options accelerate and vest immediately.

def: Describing an option or right that its holder is currently entitled to use.
ex: The warrants become exercisable only after the shares have traded above the strike price for thirty days.

def: Having the effect of increasing earnings per share or preserving an investor's proportionate stake.
ex: The convertible notes were excluded from the calculation because they were antidilutive.

def: The restructuring of a public body or partnership into a company governed by company law.
ex: Corporatisation of the port authority preceded its eventual sale to private investors.

def: Not formed as a legal company and so lacking separate legal personality.
ex: As an unincorporated association, the club could not hold property in its own name.

def: An additional benefit added to an offer to make it more attractive to shareholders.
ex: The bidder added a special dividend as a sweetener to win over reluctant investors.

def: The lending of money at unlawfully or unreasonably high rates of interest.
ex: The payday lender faced charges of usury once the true annual rate on its loans came to light.

def: Charging or involving interest at an unlawfully or exorbitantly high rate.
ex: The court struck down the usurious terms and allowed the borrower to repay only the principal.

def: The pooling of income-producing assets such as loans and their conversion into tradeable securities.
ex: The mortgage lender used securitisation to move billions of loans off its balance sheet.

def: To convert a pool of loans or receivables into marketable securities.
ex: The car-finance arm plans to securitise its auto loans to raise fresh capital.

def: The repayment of a loan, in whole or in part, before its scheduled due date.
ex: The facility agreement imposed a fee on any voluntary prepayment within the first two years.

def: The act of borrowing funds that are available under an agreed credit facility.
ex: No drawdown could be made until the borrower had satisfied every condition precedent.

def: A person who holds a charge, mortgage, or other interest burdening another's property.
ex: The second encumbrancer had to wait until the first mortgagee was paid in full.

def: The purchase of an exporter's medium-term receivables at a discount, without recourse to the exporter.
ex: The machinery exporter turned to forfaiting to remove the credit risk of its overseas buyer.

def: The person to whom a cheque or bill of exchange is transferred by endorsement.
ex: The endorsee presented the cheque for payment only to find the account had been frozen.

def: The quality of an instrument that allows it to be transferred so that the holder takes good title free of prior defects.
ex: Crossing the cheque with the words 'not negotiable' removed its negotiability.

def: The party, usually a bank, directed to pay the sum stated on a cheque or bill of exchange.
ex: The drawee bank refused payment because the signature did not match its records.

def: To refuse to accept or pay a cheque or bill of exchange when it is duly presented.
ex: The bank dishonoured the cheque for insufficient funds, triggering a claim against the drawer.

def: The drawee of a bill of exchange who has signed it to signify agreement to pay.
ex: Once the importer signed the bill as acceptor, it became primarily liable on the instrument.

def: The splitting of large cash sums into many small deposits to avoid reporting thresholds.
ex: Investigators traced the smurfing scheme to dozens of deposits made just below the reporting limit.

def: A reduction applied to the value of an asset used as collateral, or a forced write-down of a creditor's claim.
ex: The central bank applied a steep haircut to the corporate bonds offered as collateral.

def: The provision of collateral worth more than the debt it secures, as a form of credit enhancement.
ex: Overcollateralisation gave the senior noteholders a cushion against early defaults in the loan pool.

def: The sale of a financial product to a customer for whom it is unsuitable or on misleading terms.
ex: The banks paid billions in compensation for the mis-selling of payment protection insurance.

def: The bypassing of banks and other intermediaries so that borrowers raise funds directly from investors.
ex: Regulators worried that disintermediation was pushing risk into the less supervised shadow-banking sector.

def: The profit a government or central bank makes from issuing currency above its cost of production.
ex: Economists debated whether the central bank's seigniorage should be returned to the treasury.

def: The reversal of a card payment by the issuing bank following a successful customer dispute.
ex: The retailer lost the sale and paid a fee when the customer's chargeback was upheld.

def: The fraudulent use of cheques drawn between accounts to exploit clearing delays and create false balances.
ex: The auditors uncovered a kiting scheme that inflated the firm's cash by moving cheques between three banks.

def: The withdrawal of a currency unit or coin from its status as legal tender.
ex: The sudden demonetisation of high-value notes left millions queuing outside banks.

def: Relating to rules that require financial institutions to hold enough capital and liquidity to remain sound.
ex: The regulator tightened prudential requirements after several lenders breached their capital buffers.

def: Concerned with safeguarding the stability of the financial system as a whole rather than individual firms.
ex: Loan-to-income caps on mortgages are a classic macroprudential tool.

def: The setting aside of funds by a lender to cover expected losses on its loans.
ex: Higher provisioning against bad commercial loans wiped out the bank's quarterly profit.

def: The period allowed for payment of a bill of exchange, especially in foreign trade.
ex: The letter of credit allowed a usance of ninety days after shipment.

def: The transfer of title back to a borrower once a secured debt has been fully repaid.
ex: The lender issued a deed of reconveyance after the final mortgage instalment cleared.

def: Describing a security or debt that the issuer has no obligation or right to repay at a fixed date.
ex: The bank raised capital through irredeemable preference shares that count towards its core reserves.

def: The extent to which a borrower is judged able and willing to repay debts.
ex: Lenders must assess a consumer's creditworthiness before granting a loan.

def: Describing a share or bond issue for which investors have applied for fewer securities than were offered.
ex: The rights issue was undersubscribed, leaving the underwriters to take up the shortfall.

def: The replacement of an existing debt with a new loan, usually on different terms.
ex: The refinancing pushed the group's debt maturities back by five years.

def: The condition of lacking cash or assets that can be quickly sold without significant loss.
ex: The property fund suspended redemptions, citing the illiquidity of its commercial holdings.

def: The illegal practice of trading for one's own account ahead of a client's large order to profit from its price impact.
ex: The trader was dismissed after compliance detected a pattern of front-running before client block trades.

def: An investor who owns units in a unit trust or similar collective investment scheme.
ex: Unitholders were barred from withdrawing their money while the fund was gated.

def: The role or responsibility of holding and safeguarding assets on another's behalf.
ex: The pension scheme transferred custodianship of its equities to a global bank.

def: An entity that stands between buyers and sellers to guarantee and settle trades.
ex: The clearinghouse demanded extra margin from members as market volatility spiked.

def: A person who signs a document jointly with another and shares liability under it.
ex: As cosignatory to the loan, her father became liable when the repayments stopped.

def: The reduction in the real value of a currency, historically by lowering its precious-metal content.
ex: Critics accused the government of currency debasement through relentless money printing.

def: The term of a loan or financial instrument, meaning the period until it falls due for repayment.
ex: The borrower asked to extend the tenor of the facility from three to five years.

def: The act of taking on a debt or liability, often tested against limits in a financing covenant.
ex: The bond indenture contains an incurrence test that blocks new borrowing above a set leverage ratio.

def: The state of a bank account that has had no customer-initiated activity for a prolonged period.
ex: After fifteen years of dormancy, the balance was transferred to the reclaim fund.

def: The closure of a customer's accounts or refusal of banking services by a bank.
ex: New rules require banks to give clear reasons and longer notice before debanking a customer.

def: The wholesale termination of business with clients or regions deemed high risk rather than managing that risk.
ex: Charities operating in conflict zones suffered from banks' de-risking of entire jurisdictions.

def: The quality of a project or contract being sound enough to attract lenders' financing.
ex: Lenders questioned the bankability of the wind farm without a long-term offtake agreement.

def: Lacking access to the services of a bank or similar financial institution.
ex: Mobile money transformed payments for the unbanked rural population.

def: Describing a bankrupt who has not yet been released from bankruptcy and its restrictions.
ex: As an undischarged bankrupt, he could not obtain credit above a modest sum without disclosing his status.

def: A sharia-compliant financial certificate giving investors a share in an underlying asset rather than interest-bearing debt.
ex: The government issued its first sovereign sukuk to tap Gulf investors.

def: To wind up a company's affairs by selling its assets and distributing the proceeds to creditors.
ex: The court ordered the creditors to liquidate the trading subsidiary once the rescue bid collapsed.

def: The wasteful or deliberate depletion of assets so that they are unavailable to creditors.
ex: The freezing order was granted because of a real risk of dissipation before trial.

def: Able to pay all debts as they fall due and having assets exceeding liabilities.
ex: The directors signed a declaration that the company would remain solvent for the next twelve months.

def: Not easily converted into cash without a significant loss of value.
ex: Most of the estate was tied up in illiquid property holdings that would take years to sell.

def: A sale of an insolvent business arranged before an administrator is appointed and completed immediately on appointment.
ex: Critics argued the prepack let the former directors buy back the business free of its debts.

def: The conversion of assets into cash, especially by an office-holder for distribution to creditors.
ex: The liquidator's report detailed the realisation of the stock, plant and book debts.

def: Of a debt, capable of being submitted and admitted for dividend in an insolvency.
ex: The tribunal held that the contingent liability was a provable debt in the bankruptcy.

def: The conversion of debt into equity as part of a financial restructuring.
ex: The equitisation left the hedge funds owning ninety per cent of the retailer.

def: Having little or no money.
ex: Suing an impecunious defendant was pointless, since any judgment would go unpaid.

def: The total amount of money owed by a person or company.
ex: The facility agreement capped the group's financial indebtedness at three times earnings.

def: Disagreeing with a majority decision, especially as a creditor or shareholder voting against a scheme.
ex: The judge considered whether the dissentient creditors had been fairly treated under the plan.

def: Failing to provide for future needs; financially imprudent.
ex: The court found the sale improvident, as the receiver had made no attempt to market the land.

def: Capable of being converted into cash.
ex: The estimated realisable value of the stock fell far short of the outstanding debt.

def: An amount owed to a business by its customers, recorded as an asset.
ex: The invoice discounter took security over all trade receivables of the group.

def: The state in which a debtor's liabilities exceed its assets, a ground for insolvency filing in some jurisdictions.
ex: Under German law, overindebtedness obliges directors to file for insolvency within weeks.

def: Burdened with more debt than a business can sustainably service.
ex: The overleveraged buyout left the company unable to absorb even a modest fall in sales.

def: Of a debt, capable of being released when a bankrupt is discharged.
ex: Student loans are generally not dischargeable, so the debt survived the bankruptcy.

def: A creditor holding a charge over a debtor's assets as security.
ex: The qualifying floating chargeholder appointed administrators out of court within hours.

def: The extension of debt maturities without reducing principal, as a milder alternative to restructuring.
ex: The sovereign proposed a reprofiling of its bonds to avoid an outright default.

def: The margin by which a borrower remains within its financial covenants or credit limits.
ex: With covenant headroom shrinking each quarter, the board opened talks with its lenders.

def: The availability of cash or readily saleable assets to meet short-term obligations.
ex: A short-term liquidity injection from shareholders kept the company trading through the winter.

def: To treat a transaction in law as something other than what the parties labelled it.
ex: The administrator asked the court to recharacterise the sale and leaseback as a secured loan.

def: Existing or occurring before a particular event, such as the onset of insolvency.
ex: Security granted for an antecedent debt shortly before collapse may be vulnerable to challenge.

def: To squander or dispose of assets so that they are lost to creditors.
ex: The claimant feared the defendant would dissipate his assets before judgment could be enforced.

def: The assessment or sale of an asset at less than its true worth.
ex: Creditors alleged gross undervaluation in the sale of the brand to a connected party.

def: In Scots law, to make a person bankrupt by placing their estate under the control of a trustee.
ex: The sheriff granted the petition to sequestrate the estate of the property developer.

def: The improper use of funds or property for a purpose other than that intended.
ex: The director faced a claim for misapplication of company money used to settle his personal debts.

def: A legal arrangement placing a failing institution under the control of an appointed custodian.
ex: The mortgage agencies were placed into conservatorship at the height of the financial crisis.

def: A person or body appointed to manage and preserve the assets of a failing institution.
ex: The regulator acted as conservator, preserving the lender's assets while a buyer was found.

def: The office or period of administration of a trustee over an estate.
ex: During his trusteeship, the trustee recovered several properties transferred to the bankrupt's relatives.

def: To remove a company or entity from an official register.
ex: The liquidator applied to deregister the company once the final distribution had been paid.

def: In proportion to the size of each claim; on an equal proportional basis.
ex: Unsecured creditors were paid rateably from the funds remaining after the preferential claims.

def: The extent to which a debt or asset value can realistically be recovered.
ex: Doubts about the recoverability of the loan book prompted a fresh round of impairments.

def: A person who, without authority, takes it upon themselves to deal with trust or estate property.
ex: The nephew who sold his late aunt's car was treated as an intermeddler and held liable as executor de son tort.

def: To interfere with property or affairs one has no authority to handle.
ex: By paying the estate's creditors before probate, he had intermeddled and lost the right to renounce.

def: A person who holds and exercises a power of appointment over property.
ex: The deed named the settlor's widow as appointor, able to replace the trustees at will.

def: A person who receives a gift or to whom a power is granted.
ex: As donee of the power, the trustee could allocate income among the grandchildren.

def: To formally give up a right, office, or claim.
ex: The appointed executor renounced probate, leaving the residuary beneficiary to apply for letters of administration.

def: The transfer of property from an existing trust into a new settlement on fresh terms.
ex: HMRC argued that the variation amounted to a resettlement, triggering a fresh charge to tax.

def: Unfair or unjust, especially in a way equity will not permit.
ex: The court held it would be inequitable to allow the landlord to resile from his assurance.

def: The quality of failing to plan or provide for the future.
ex: A protective trust was chosen precisely because of the beneficiary's well-documented improvidence.

def: Free from restriction or control.
ex: The trust deed gave the trustees unfettered discretion over the timing of distributions.

def: To restrict or limit the free exercise of a power or discretion.
ex: Trustees must not fetter their discretion by promising in advance how they will vote.

def: To deprive someone of a right or claim they would otherwise have.
ex: His own misconduct disentitled him to the equitable relief he sought.

def: A party who takes over another's rights against a third person through subrogation.

def: In a fair and impartial manner, or according to the principles of equity.

def: A party granted the right to operate a business using another's brand and system.
ex: The Franchisee shall operate the outlet strictly in accordance with the Operations Manual.

def: To rely on or call into operation a contractual right or provision.
ex: The Supplier sought to invoke the force majeure clause after the port closures delayed shipment.

def: The freedom to decide what should be done in a particular situation.
ex: The Company may, at its sole discretion, extend the deadline for performance.

def: To a significant degree that would affect a reasonable party's position or decision.
ex: The Buyer may terminate if the Seller's performance falls materially below the agreed service levels.

def: Harmful or unfavourable to a party's interests or position.
ex: The Purchaser may withdraw if any material adverse change affects the Target before Completion.

def: A right to receive something under the terms of an agreement.
ex: The Agent's entitlement to commission ceases on the effective date of termination.

def: Not subject to an upper limit on the amount payable or recoverable.
ex: Liability for breach of the data protection obligations shall be uncapped.

def: A minimum level that must be reached before a right or obligation applies.
ex: No claim may be brought unless the amount exceeds the threshold of ten thousand pounds.

def: To find out or establish something with certainty.

def: Involving mutual obligations undertaken by two parties.

def: To entrust the performance of a duty to another person while remaining responsible for it.
ex: The Contractor may not delegate any of its obligations without the Employer's prior written consent.

def: To engage a third party to perform part of one's own contractual obligations.
ex: The Supplier may subcontract the delivery services provided it remains liable for the subcontractor's acts.

def: To begin, especially formally or on a specified date.

def: The point at which an agreement or arrangement begins.
ex: The policy has provided cover for the premises since its inception in 2019.

def: To postpone an action, payment or event to a later time.

def: Something that obstructs or delays a party's performance.

def: An excess of cost or time beyond what was agreed or budgeted.

def: A failure to keep to an agreed timetable, resulting in delay.
ex: The Supplier shall notify the Customer promptly of any slippage against the project plan.

def: To deduct an amount owed by one party from an amount owed to it.
ex: The Customer may offset any service credits against the next invoice issued by the Supplier.

def: To refuse to give or pay something that is otherwise due.
ex: The Employer may withhold five per cent of each payment as retention until practical completion.

def: The person to whom goods are sent or delivered under a contract of carriage.
ex: Risk in the Goods shall pass to the consignee when they are unloaded at the named port.

def: The person who sends goods to another under a contract of carriage or consignment.
ex: The consignor remains the owner of the stock until the retailer has sold it to an end customer.

def: Of a quality fit to be sold in the ordinary course of trade.
ex: The Seller warrants that the Goods shall be of merchantable quality and free from material defects.

def: Kept in a form that allows independent inspection and verification.
ex: The Licensee shall maintain complete and auditable records of all sales on which royalties are payable.

def: A statute or statutory provision that has been passed into law.
ex: A reference to legislation includes any statutory modification or re-enactment of it for the time being in force.

def: A conflict between two provisions or documents that cannot both be given effect.

def: To deprive a provision or agreement of legal force.
ex: A later inconsistent clause cannot nullify the exclusion unless the parties clearly intended it to.

def: Remaining after other specific items or claims have been dealt with.
ex: Any residual liability not covered by insurance shall be shared equally between the parties.

def: A document sent in the same envelope or email as a covering letter.
ex: Please find as an enclosure a signed copy of the share purchase agreement for your records.

def: A formal confirmation that a letter, document or claim has been received.
ex: We would be grateful for your acknowledgement of this letter by return.

def: A final demand whose rejection will lead to specified action being taken.
ex: The letter amounts to an ultimatum: pay within fourteen days or proceedings will be issued.

def: To make something clear by explaining it in more detail.
ex: We should be grateful if you would elucidate the basis on which your client calculates the sum claimed.

def: To make a process happen more quickly.
ex: To expedite completion, we enclose the draft transfer for your approval.

def: In a quick and efficient manner.
ex: We trust that this matter can now be resolved expeditiously and without recourse to the courts.

def: In good time or within the required period.
ex: Your client failed to serve the notice timeously and the option has therefore lapsed.

def: Coming or happening later than it should have.
ex: Your belated response does not alter our client's position that the contract has been terminated.

def: A short summary of the essential points of a longer text.
ex: I set out below a brief precis of the key terms of the proposed lease.

def: The greeting at the opening of a letter, such as Dear Sir or Madam.
ex: Where the recipient is unnamed, the salutation should read Dear Sirs and the letter close with Yours faithfully.

def: The closing phrase of a letter before the signature.
ex: A letter beginning with a named salutation takes the valediction Yours sincerely.

def: To inform someone formally of a fact or development.
ex: We will keep you apprised of any developments in the negotiations with the landlord.

def: To supply someone with information or documents.
ex: Kindly furnish us with copies of all invoices relied upon in support of the claim.

def: To provide evidence that proves a claim or statement is true.
ex: Your client has produced no documents to substantiate the alleged losses.

def: A claim that someone has done something wrong, typically made without proof.
ex: Our client categorically denies the allegation of breach set out in your letter of 3 May.

def: An assertion or argument put forward in a dispute.
ex: It is our contention that the limitation clause does not apply to deliberate breaches.

def: To admit, often reluctantly, that something is true or valid.
ex: Our client is prepared to concede that delivery was late but denies that any loss resulted.

def: Most noticeable or important.
ex: The salient terms of the agreement are summarised in the schedule to this letter.

def: Directly relevant to the matter being considered.
ex: Please forward any correspondence pertinent to the dispute so that we can assess your position.

def: Relevant and appropriate to a subject under consideration.
ex: The earlier negotiations are not germane to the construction of the signed contract.

def: Having knowledge or awareness of something.
ex: Our client was at all times cognisant of the restrictive covenant affecting the property.

def: Familiar with and knowledgeable about a subject.
ex: As you will be conversant with the relevant regulations, we do not propose to repeat them here.

def: Without intention, by accident or oversight.
ex: A privileged email was inadvertently included in the bundle and we request its immediate return.

def: An error in a printed or written document, or a note correcting it.
ex: Please note the erratum in paragraph 4 of our previous letter, where the date should read 12 June.

def: Having built up over a period of time, especially of interest or rights.
ex: The sum claimed includes accrued interest at the contractual rate from the due date.

def: To repay money that someone has spent or lost.
ex: Our client is willing to reimburse your reasonable costs of the inspection.

def: To stop doing something, especially when required to do so.
ex: We hereby demand that your client cease and desist from using our client's trade mark.

def: In a way that leaves no doubt.
ex: Our client unequivocally rejects the offer contained in your letter of 8 March.

def: Absolutely clear and direct, allowing no exception.
ex: We require a categorical assurance that the confidential information has been destroyed.

def: In a way that is understood or implied without being stated.
ex: By continuing to accept deliveries, your client tacitly accepted the revised terms.

def: From that thing or source just mentioned.
ex: Our client accepts liability for the defect and any loss arising therefrom.

def: Mentioned later or below in the same document.
ex: Please provide the undermentioned documents before the meeting on Friday.

def: Attached or added at the end of a document.
ex: The appended schedule sets out the payment dates agreed between the parties.

def: To state an opinion formally.
ex: Counsel has opined that the restraint of trade clause is likely to be unenforceable.

def: A letter, especially a long or official one.
ex: Your client's latest missive raises no new points and does not merit a detailed reply.

def: Showing respect and politeness, sometimes excessively.
ex: Letters to the court should be courteous but need not be overly deferential.

def: In a way that insists on immediate attention and allows no refusal.
ex: Your client peremptorily terminated the agreement without giving the notice required by clause 15.

def: The quality of being open, honest and frank.
ex: In the interests of candour, I must advise you that your prospects at trial are no better than even.

def: Direct and outspoken in stating one's views.
ex: I would recommend a forthright reply that makes our client's position clear from the outset.

def: Careful to consider risks and consequences before acting or speaking.
ex: You should be circumspect in any discussions with the other side until the settlement is signed.

def: Showing good judgement and sense.
ex: A judicious offer to settle at this stage may protect you against an adverse costs order.

def: Having only one possible meaning.
ex: The wording of clause 7 is unambiguous and plainly excludes liability for indirect loss.

def: Expressed clearly and easy to understand.
ex: Clients appreciate a lucid explanation of their options free from technical jargon.

def: Briefly and clearly expressed.
ex: Please keep your advice to the board succinct, with a short summary of the main risks.

def: Producing a beneficial effect, often through an unpleasant experience.
ex: The judgment is a salutary reminder that notice provisions must be strictly observed.

def: Serving as a warning.
ex: I add a cautionary note: any admission made in correspondence may be relied upon in court.

def: Likely to have unfortunate consequences and therefore unwise.
ex: It would be inadvisable for you to sign the guarantee before we have reviewed it.

def: To discuss or examine a matter thoroughly.
ex: The options for an early resolution were canvassed at our meeting last week.

def: To say something again for emphasis or clarity.
ex: We reiterate that our client reserves all its rights in relation to the defective goods.

def: To explain or set out an idea or position in detail.
ex: Counsel will expound the legal basis of the claim in the skeleton argument.

def: To list things individually, especially charges on a bill.
ex: Please itemise the disbursements included in your interim invoice.

def: False or lacking a genuine basis, though appearing valid.
ex: Your client's counterclaim is spurious and appears designed solely to delay payment.

def: Not supported by any evidence or facts.
ex: The allegations of misconduct against our client are entirely baseless and are denied.

def: Having no basis in fact.
ex: We consider your client's concerns about the title to be unfounded.

def: Concerning the essential substance of a matter rather than procedure.
ex: We will provide a substantive response to your letter once we have taken our client's instructions.

def: Serving to prove a case or settle a question beyond doubt.
ex: The signed delivery note is conclusive evidence that the goods were received in good condition.

def: Protected from disclosure in legal proceedings because of a lawyer and client relationship.
ex: This letter is privileged and confidential and must not be forwarded to third parties.

def: Claimed to be something, though this is doubted or disputed.
ex: Our client does not accept the purported notice of termination served on 2 April.

def: To read something carefully and thoroughly.
ex: Having perused the draft agreement, we have a number of comments, which are set out below.

def: The act of reading something carefully.
ex: We enclose the draft lease for your perusal and comment.

def: Lacking care or attention to duty.
ex: We would be remiss if we did not warn you of the costs risk of proceeding to trial.

def: In a friendly and cooperative way, without serious disagreement.
ex: Our client remains hopeful that the dispute can be resolved amicably through mediation.

def: An indication or formal notification of something.
ex: We have received no intimation from your client that the deadline would not be met.

def: An approach or proposal made to open negotiations.
ex: Our client would welcome any overture from your client towards a negotiated settlement.

def: Apparently or as stated, though perhaps not actually.
ex: The payment was ostensibly a consultancy fee, but we believe it was in fact a commission.

def: Without any conditions or limitations.
ex: Our client unconditionally accepts your client's offer of £25,000 in full and final settlement.

def: A person or company to whom money is owed by another party.
ex: The administrator must notify every known creditor of the company within fourteen days of appointment.

def: A person or company that owes money to another party.
ex: The Debtor shall repay the outstanding sum in twelve equal monthly instalments.

def: Describing a debt or loan that is not backed by any charge over the borrower's assets.
ex: Unsecured creditors are likely to recover only a small fraction of what they are owed.

def: Not revealed or made known to the other party or the public.
ex: An agent acting for an undisclosed principal may still be personally liable on the contract.

def: The total value of a company's issued shares or the structure of its capital.
ex: The target's market capitalisation fell sharply after the profit warning was announced.

def: An agreement to take up and pay for newly issued shares in a company.
ex: The investor's subscription for 50,000 ordinary shares is conditional on board approval.

def: A person or entity that owns shares in a company, used especially in American usage.
ex: The merger requires approval by a majority of the stockholders of the Delaware parent.

def: Postponed to a later date, or ranking behind other claims for payment.
ex: Part of the purchase price will be paid as deferred consideration twelve months after Completion.

def: The bank that organises a syndicated loan and negotiates its terms with the borrower.
ex: The mandated lead arranger will distribute the facility to a syndicate of eight banks.

def: Describing a loan provided jointly by a group of lenders under one agreement.
ex: The acquisition was financed through a £300 million syndicated term loan.

def: Failing to make a payment or perform a duty by the date it falls due.
ex: Delinquent accounts more than ninety days overdue will be referred to the collections team.

def: Harm or damage to a person's legal rights or interests.
ex: The settlement offer was made without prejudice to the company's right to claim further damages.

def: The room where a company's directors meet, or the senior management of a company more generally.
ex: A boardroom dispute between the two founders has left the company in deadlock.

def: A person appointed to act and vote in place of a director who cannot attend a meeting.
ex: Any director may appoint an alternate to attend board meetings in his absence.

def: A party that has the right to propose or appoint a person to an office.
ex: Each investor director may be removed only by written notice from his nominator.

def: A formal document creating an organisation and setting out its rights and purposes.
ex: The institute was incorporated by royal charter rather than under the Companies Act.

def: Officially examined and verified by an independent accountant.
ex: The Seller warrants that the audited accounts give a true and fair view of the Company's financial position.

def: Given without any reservation, especially of an auditor's opinion on accounts.
ex: The auditors issued an unqualified opinion on the group's financial statements.

def: To bring the legal existence of a company or partnership formally to an end.
ex: The partnership shall be dissolved on the death or bankruptcy of any partner.

def: Capable of being approved after the event so that it becomes legally valid.
ex: A breach of duty involving fraud on the minority is not ratifiable by an ordinary resolution.

def: The holding by a company of its own bought-back shares, which are kept rather than cancelled.
ex: The repurchased shares will be held in treasury and may later be sold for cash.

def: The amount by which the price paid for a share exceeds its nominal value.
ex: The shares were issued at a premium of £4.50, which must be credited to the share premium account.

def: Profits and other sums retained by a company rather than distributed to shareholders.
ex: A dividend may only be paid out of distributable reserves shown in the relevant accounts.

def: A person to whom newly issued shares have been allocated by a company.
ex: Share certificates shall be delivered to each allottee within two months of allotment.

def: The person on whose behalf an agent acts and who is bound by the agent's authorised acts.
ex: The Agent shall not hold itself out as having authority to bind the Principal to any contract.

def: Describing a debt that is backed by a charge or other security over the borrower's assets.
ex: As a secured lender, the bank will be repaid from the proceeds of the charged property first.

def: Describing a charge over a changing class of assets that the company may deal with until it crystallises.
ex: The debenture creates a fixed charge over the premises and a floating charge over the stock.

def: Describing a person not formally appointed whose instructions the directors are accustomed to follow.
ex: The majority investor risked being treated as a shadow director because the board acted on its every instruction.

def: Agreed to by every person entitled to vote.
ex: Any change to the reserved matters requires the unanimous written consent of the shareholders.

def: Describing shares or a company not admitted to trading on a stock exchange.
ex: Valuing unlisted shares is difficult because there is no open market price.

def: A company or body that creates and offers securities such as shares or bonds.
ex: The Issuer shall publish a prospectus approved by the competent authority before the offer opens.

def: The sale of new securities directly to selected investors rather than to the general public.
ex: The company raised £20 million through a private placement with institutional investors.

def: To combine shares into fewer shares of a larger nominal value, or to combine accounts of a group.

def: The splitting of existing shares into a greater number of shares of lower nominal value.
ex: Following the subdivision, each £1 share became four shares of 25p each.

def: The currency or face value in which a share, bond or note is expressed.
ex: The notes will be issued in a minimum denomination of €100,000.

def: To buy back shares or repay a bond on the terms set out when it was issued.

def: The buying back by a company of its own issued shares.

def: Describing shares held and transferred electronically without a paper certificate.
ex: Shares held in uncertificated form will be credited to the holder's account in the settlement system.

def: Capable of being legally passed from one owner to another.
ex: The rights under this licence are personal to the Licensee and are not transferable.

def: Describing an instrument that can be transferred by delivery or endorsement so the holder gains good title.

def: Sums owed to a business by its customers for goods or services already supplied.
ex: The company assigned its trade receivables to the factor in return for immediate cash.

def: Sums a business owes to its suppliers and other creditors.
ex: The purchase price will be adjusted for any trade payables outstanding at Completion.

def: The extent to which a party is at risk of financial loss or liability.
ex: The cap in clause 12 limits the Seller's total exposure under the warranties to the purchase price.

def: Describing assets without physical form, such as goodwill or intellectual property.
ex: Much of the target's value lies in intangible assets, particularly its patents and brand.

def: An expert assessment of how much a business, share or asset is worth.
ex: If the parties cannot agree a price, the fair value of the shares shall be determined by an independent valuation.

def: A neutral third party who helps disputing parties negotiate a voluntary resolution.
ex: The mediator met each side privately before proposing a framework for settlement.

def: The formal written statements in which each party sets out its case before a civil trial.
ex: The defendant sought permission to amend its pleadings to add a defence of limitation.

def: The court or tribunal in which a dispute is heard and determined.
ex: The clause designates the English courts as the exclusive forum for any dispute arising under this Agreement.

def: The process of taking legal action through the courts to resolve a dispute.
ex: We would advise exploring mediation before committing the company to protracted litigation.

def: A person who has been found guilty of contempt of court.

def: The offence of disobeying or showing disrespect for the authority of a court.
ex: Failure to comply with this order may result in proceedings for contempt of court.

def: A penalty imposed by a court for failing to comply with a rule, order or procedural requirement.
ex: The judge imposed a costs sanction on the claimant for its late disclosure of documents.

def: The overturning of a lower court's decision by a higher court on appeal.

def: The obligation on a party to prove a disputed fact or assertion in proceedings.
ex: The burden of proving that the loss was caused by the breach rests with the claimant.

def: To calculate or express the amount of a loss or claim in monetary terms.
ex: Our forensic accountants are still working to quantify the client's lost profits.

def: To become involved in existing proceedings as a third party with an interest in the outcome.

def: To bring a legal right, claim or liability to an end.
ex: Payment of the settlement sum shall fully extinguish all claims between the parties arising from the project.

def: The taking of property into legal custody, typically to enforce a judgment or preserve evidence.
ex: The enforcement officer authorised the seizure of the debtor's vehicles to satisfy the outstanding judgment.

def: Lasting much longer than expected or desirable.
ex: Both parties wished to avoid protracted proceedings that would damage their commercial relationship.

def: Relating to the rules and steps by which a case is conducted rather than its legal merits.
ex: The appeal was allowed on a procedural irregularity in the way the evidence had been admitted.

def: To reverse or set aside a decision of a lower court or tribunal.
ex: The Supreme Court overturned the ruling, holding that the exclusion clause was effective.

def: To set out a claim or defence formally in a statement of case.
ex: The claimant has pleaded misrepresentation in the alternative to breach of contract.

def: Disputed by the other party and therefore requiring determination by a court or tribunal.
ex: The quantum of the claim remains contested, although liability has been admitted.

def: Not disputed or challenged by any party.
ex: As the application was uncontested, the judge granted the order without a hearing.

def: So clear or certain that it cannot be disputed.
ex: The signed delivery notes provide incontestable evidence that the goods were received on time.

def: To uphold the decision of a lower court on appeal.
ex: The Court of Appeal affirmed the judgment and dismissed the appeal with costs.

def: To make a contract, clause or decision legally ineffective.
ex: A finding of undue influence would invalidate the guarantee in its entirety.

def: To give a false or misleading account of a fact, especially to induce someone to enter a contract.
ex: The seller misrepresented the company's turnover during pre-contractual negotiations.

def: Illegal or improper conduct.
ex: The settlement was agreed without any admission of wrongdoing by the defendant.

def: Done with the intention of causing harm or without legal justification.
ex: The claimant alleges that the defendant brought the earlier proceedings for a malicious purpose.

def: The amount by which a sum or quantity falls short of what is required or expected.

def: A payment of more than the amount actually due.
ex: The supplier must refund any overpayment within fourteen days of written notice.

def: An unexpected gain, especially one that would leave a claimant better off than if the wrong had not occurred.

def: Compensation that exceeds the actual loss suffered.
ex: Credit must be given for the insurance payout to avoid overcompensation of the claimant.

def: Occurring between a wrongful act and the resulting loss in a way that may break the chain of causation.

def: Something that discourages a person from acting in a particular way.

def: Relating to the formal process of judging and deciding a dispute.

def: An official order issued by a court, especially one granting equitable relief.
ex: The court issued a decree of specific performance compelling the vendor to complete the sale.

def: An authoritative decision made by a judge or tribunal on a point of law or procedure.

def: Sufficiently different on its facts that an earlier case need not be followed as a precedent.

def: The quality of a decision being capable of challenge before a higher court.
ex: The parties disagreed over the appealability of the interim award under the Arbitration Act.

def: Lasting indefinitely, especially of an injunction granted as final relief after trial.

def: Coming before the main hearing and dealing with an issue that must be resolved first.

def: Unable to reach agreement because neither side will give way.

def: To refer a dispute to a higher level of management or a more formal resolution process.

def: To negotiate the terms of an existing agreement again in order to change them.

def: To make conflicting positions, accounts or interests consistent with one another.

def: The restoration of an amicable relationship between parties after a dispute.
ex: Early mediation offers the best prospect of reconciliation and preserving the joint venture.

def: Treating all parties equally and without favour.
ex: Each arbitrator shall be and remain impartial and independent of the parties.

def: In a way that pursues legal proceedings without merit, mainly to harass or burden the other party.
ex: The court found that the litigant had acted vexatiously by issuing repeated claims on the same facts.

def: Not supported or proved by evidence.
ex: The counterclaim rests on unsubstantiated assertions and should be struck out.

def: Capable of being resolved by arbitration rather than only by a court.
ex: The tribunal held that the competition law claims were arbitrable and fell within the scope of the clause.

def: To prohibit a party by court order from doing a particular act.
ex: The court granted an interim injunction to restrain the former director from soliciting the company's clients.

def: To force a party by legal authority to do something.
ex: The claimant has applied for an order to compel the defendant to produce the missing board minutes.

def: To take out a new or further mortgage on a property, usually to replace an existing loan or release equity.

def: The act of occupying land or a building without the owner's permission or any legal right to do so.

def: The system by which a planning authority designates areas of land for particular permitted uses.

def: A qualified professional who assesses the market value of land, buildings or other assets.

def: The legal removal of a tenant or occupier from a property.
ex: The tenant argued that the eviction was unlawful because no valid notice had been served.

def: Done without force, violence or dispute, as in peaceable re-entry or possession of land.

def: Describing property that is subject to a charge, lien or other third-party right.

def: To let a property again to a new tenant after a previous tenancy has ended.
ex: The landlord must take reasonable steps to relet the premises in order to mitigate its loss.

def: In a state of disrepair or ruin as a result of age or neglect.
ex: The tenant handed back the premises in a dilapidated condition, in clear breach of the repairing covenant.

def: A smaller building, such as a shed or garage, separate from but belonging to a main building.
ex: The sale includes the farmhouse together with all outbuildings shown edged red on the plan.

def: Describing premises that have been granted to a tenant under a lease.
ex: The Tenant shall keep the demised premises in good and substantial repair throughout the Term.

def: The exercise or possession of a legal right, especially a tenant's right to use land without interference.
ex: The landlord's building works were a breach of the covenant for quiet enjoyment.

def: The practice of contracting out work or services previously performed in-house to an external provider.
ex: The outsourcing of the payroll function triggered a transfer of the affected employees to the new supplier.

def: A temporary or permanent suspension of employment because there is insufficient work.
ex: An employee laid off for four consecutive weeks may be entitled to claim a redundancy payment.

def: Relating to or involving formal discussion with those affected before a decision is taken.
ex: The employer failed to follow a meaningful consultative process before announcing the closure.

def: Describing a workforce or workplace whose employees belong to a recognised trade union.

def: The act of enticing employees or clients away from a rival or former employer.

def: A working arrangement allowing employees to vary their start and finish times within agreed limits.

def: Working remotely from home or another location using electronic communication.

def: The degree to which a person has the skills and qualities that make them suitable for employment.

def: The formal process of introducing a new employee to their role and the organisation.

def: Failure by an employee to reach the standard of work reasonably required for their role.

def: A defined skill or behaviour against which an employee's performance is measured.
ex: Candidates were scored against six core competencies set out in the job description.

def: Serious enough to justify the termination of a person's employment.
ex: The handbook lists falsification of expense claims as a dismissible offence.

def: Arising from or agreed under a binding contract.
ex: The bonus scheme was found to be contractual rather than discretionary, so the employer was obliged to pay it.

def: The list of a company's employees and the total amount it pays them in wages and salaries.
ex: The transferee inherited a payroll of 140 staff under the transfer regulations.

def: Equality of pay, status or treatment between comparable groups or individuals.
ex: The union demanded pay parity for agency workers performing the same work as permanent staff.

def: Describing leave or treatment granted in response to personal hardship such as bereavement.
ex: Employees are entitled to up to five days' compassionate leave following the death of a close relative.

def: Protected by a patent granted to its inventor or owner.
ex: The licensee may manufacture the patented product only within the agreed territory.

def: In patent law, involving a step that would not be obvious to a person skilled in the relevant field.
ex: The patent was revoked because the claimed process lacked an inventive step over the prior art.

def: Describing a right that has ceased to have effect, typically because a fee or step was not taken in time.
ex: The patent lapsed when the proprietor failed to pay the fourth-year renewal fee.

def: Registered or used as a trade mark identifying the commercial origin of goods or services.
ex: The distributor may use the trademarked name only in the form approved by the Licensor.

def: Likely to mislead the public as to the nature, quality or origin of goods or services.
ex: The application was refused because the mark was deceptive as to the geographical origin of the wine.

def: To damage the reputation of a well-known mark by associating it with something unsavoury or inferior.
ex: The claimant argued that use of its logo on cheap novelty goods would tarnish the reputation of the brand.

def: An exclusively aural fixation of sounds, such as a sound recording, protected under neighbouring rights.
ex: Producers of phonograms enjoy the exclusive right to authorise the reproduction of their recordings.

def: Relating to the layout and appearance of printed text, which can attract its own copyright.
ex: The publisher owns copyright in the typographical arrangement of the published edition.

def: A licensing approach that permits free use and modification of a work on condition that derivative works are shared on the same terms.
ex: Incorporating code subject to a copyleft licence may oblige the company to release its own source code.

def: Incapable of being lawfully transferred to another person.
ex: Moral rights are unassignable, although the author may waive them in writing.

def: Published or created under a false or assumed name.
ex: Copyright in a pseudonymous work expires seventy years after it is first made available to the public.

def: Made, copied or distributed illegally without the authorisation of the rights holder.
ex: Customs officers seized over two thousand bootleg recordings of the band's live performances.

def: Reproduced and distributed in breach of copyright.
ex: The defendant sold pirated copies of the software through an online marketplace.

def: Describing goods, copies or acts that violate another's intellectual property rights.
ex: The court ordered the delivery up and destruction of all infringing articles held by the defendant.

def: To convert machine-readable object code back into a form of source code that humans can read.
ex: The licensee shall not decompile the Software except to the extent permitted by law to achieve interoperability.

def: The commercial use of an asset, especially intellectual property, to generate revenue.
ex: The Licensee shall use all reasonable endeavours to promote the commercial exploitation of the Licensed Technology.

def: To manage or develop a product, invention or right so as to make a profit from it.
ex: The university granted the spin-out company an exclusive licence to commercialise the patented compound.

def: A written statement of the facts and arguments of a case submitted to a court, especially an appellate one.
ex: Counsel spent the weekend tightening the factum before filing it with the Court of Appeal.

def: The place where a legally significant event, such as a crime or accident, occurred.
ex: The jury was taken to view the locus before closing speeches began.

def: A warrant directing a jailer to receive and hold a prisoner in custody.
ex: The clerk issued the mittimus, and the defendant was led down to the cells.

def: A constitutional right to reject a decision or proposal made by a law-making body.
ex: The governor used her veto to block the controversial housing bill.

def: A court of justice, or the body of officials through which a sovereign or the Pope governs.
ex: Medieval disputes over land were frequently settled in the king's curia.

def: A woman appointed by a court to manage the estate of a person who died without a valid will.
ex: As administratrix, the widow had to settle the debts before distributing anything.

def: A woman who brings or instigates a criminal prosecution, traditionally the complainant in a sexual offence case.
ex: Older law reports refer to the complainant simply as the prosecutrix.

def: An error in a published document that has been formally corrected, or the notice listing such corrections.
ex: The tribunal issued a corrigendum after the judgment misstated the award by a decimal place.

def: To suspend criminal proceedings on a charge indefinitely, or to mark an altered passage so that it is kept as originally written.
ex: The prosecution agreed to stet the remaining counts once he pleaded to the main charge.

def: Historically the endorsement a grand jury wrote on a bill it rejected, and now an ignorant or foolish person.
ex: The grand jury returned an ignoramus, and the indictment collapsed before trial.

def: In exactly the same words as were originally used.
ex: The stenographer recorded the witness's outburst verbatim.

def: Used in citations to indicate that a point is found at many places throughout a cited work.
ex: The footnote cited the treatise on restitution, passim, rather than a single page.

def: Used in legal writing to refer the reader to an earlier part of the same text.
ex: For the facts of the earlier appeal, see the discussion supra.

def: Used in legal writing to refer the reader to a later part of the same text.
ex: The limitation point is addressed infra, after the analysis of liability.

def: A false or assumed name used by a person, especially one recorded in legal proceedings.
ex: The indictment listed the defendant together with three known aliases.

def: In civil law, deliberate fraud or wrongful intent, as distinct from mere negligence.
ex: Because the seller acted with dolus, the exclusion clause could not protect him.

def: A Roman magistrate who administered justice and whose edicts shaped the development of Roman law.
ex: Many equitable remedies trace their origin to the edicts of the urban praetor.

def: Loss or harm suffered by a person, especially as an element of a claim for damages.
ex: Without proof of damnum, the claim for compensation was bound to fail.

def: An infringement of a legal right, whether or not it causes actual loss.
ex: Trespass is actionable as an injuria even when the land suffers no damage at all.

def: The legal bond that ties parties to an obligation, binding one to perform for the other.
ex: Roman jurists described an obligation as a vinculum juris between creditor and debtor.

def: An expert in law, especially one whose opinions on points of law carry authority.
ex: The government sought the opinion of a leading jurisconsult on the treaty's validity.

def: A body of citizens summoned by a sheriff to help keep the peace or pursue a suspect.
ex: The sheriff raised a posse to track the escaped prisoners into the hills.

def: In Scots and civil law, the share of a deceased parent's movable estate to which children are entitled regardless of the will.
ex: Although disinherited by the will, the son claimed his legitim from the estate.

def: Historically, a personal chattel that caused a death and was forfeited to the Crown for pious uses.
ex: The cart that crushed the labourer was declared a deodand and seized by the coroner.

def: Absolute ownership of property, as recognised in Roman and civil law.
ex: Possession may be transferred by lease, but dominium remains with the owner.

def: Supreme governmental power, including the authority to command and to enforce the law.
ex: The court distinguished the state's imperium from its private rights as a landowner.

def: Joint sovereignty over a territory exercised by two or more states.
ex: For decades the islands were governed as an Anglo-French condominium.

def: In the same source as the one cited immediately before.
ex: The second quotation came from the same judgment, so the footnote simply read ibidem.

def: Without charge or payment.
ex: The solicitor agreed to draft the charity's constitution gratis.

def: A historical writ or notice directing a sheriff or company to restrain property, such as shares, from being dealt with.
ex: A notice in the nature of a distringas stopped the company registering any transfer of the shares.

def: A historical writ of execution allowing a judgment creditor to take possession of the debtor's land until the debt was paid.
ex: Unable to seize his goods, the creditor sued out an elegit against the debtor's estate.

def: A writ sending a case back from a higher court to a lower one with an order to proceed to judgment.
ex: Finding no error, the superior court issued a procedendo returning the matter below.

def: A remark made by a judge in passing that is not essential to the decision and so is not binding.
ex: The comment on frustration was mere obiter, though later courts found it persuasive.

def: A person who undertakes to act on behalf of another under a mandate, often without payment.
ex: As mandatary, he was bound to follow his principal's instructions to the letter.

def: The clause in a deed specifying the tenure by which the granted land is to be held.
ex: The habendum and tenendum together set out the estate granted and how it was held.

def: A person who leaves a legacy of personal property by will.
ex: The legator directed that his library pass to the university after his death.

def: The acquisition of ownership of a thing because it has become inseparably attached to another thing one owns.
ex: Paint applied to another's canvas was traditionally lost to its owner by accessio.

def: The acquisition of ownership by creating a new thing from materials belonging to another.
ex: Whether wine pressed from stolen grapes belongs to the maker is a classic problem of specificatio.

def: A historical common law action to recover damages for breach of an informal promise or contract.
ex: Modern contract law grew largely out of the old action of assumpsit.

def: The person who ultimately benefits from a fideicommissum, receiving property held by an intermediate heir.
ex: On the heir's death, the estate passed to the fideicommissary named in the will.

def: In Roman law, property that a father or master allowed a son or slave to manage as if it were their own.
ex: The slave traded with his peculium and eventually saved enough to buy his freedom.

def: A gratuitous loan of an item that must be returned in its original form after use.
ex: Lending a neighbour your ladder for the weekend is a textbook commodatum.

def: A loan of consumable goods, such as money or grain, to be repaid in equivalent kind and quantity.
ex: Since the borrowed wheat would be eaten, the arrangement was a mutuum rather than a loan for use.

def: In Roman law, the wrongful handling of another's property with intent to gain, broadly equivalent to theft.
ex: Using a borrowed horse for a longer journey than agreed could amount to furtum.

def: Law in the abstract, or a particular legal right recognised by a legal system.
ex: Scholars debate whether the right of passage is a true jus or merely a privilege.

def: Having made a valid will before death.
ex: Because she died testate, the estate passed according to her own wishes.

def: A woman appointed by a court to manage the property or affairs of a person unable to do so.
ex: The court named his sister as curatrix of his estate after the accident.

def: A woman appointed as the legal guardian of a minor and their property.
ex: Under the civil code, the mother served as tutrix until the children came of age.

def: Used in brackets after a quoted word to show it has been reproduced exactly, including any error.
ex: The letter read that the tenant had been "evicted illegaly " by the landlord.

def: Used in formal documents to introduce a more precise statement of what has just been mentioned.
