def: The doctrine that Union law prevails over any conflicting provision of national law.
ex: Invoking supremacy, the national court disapplied the incompatible statute.

def: The principle that Union law takes precedence over conflicting rules of national law.
ex: The primacy of Union law obliges national courts to set aside contrary domestic rules.

def: A member of a parliamentary committee or a court designated to prepare a report or draft on a given file.
ex: The rapporteur presented her draft report on the data-protection regulation.

def: An informal tripartite negotiation between the Parliament, the Council and the Commission to agree the text of legislation.
ex: The compromise text emerged from months of trilogue negotiations.

def: The process by which a state becomes a member of the European Union.
ex: Croatia's accession brought the membership to twenty-eight states.

def: The expansion of the Union through the admission of new Member States.
ex: The 2004 enlargement admitted ten new Member States at once.

def: The alignment of national laws to a common Union standard.
ex: Full harmonisation leaves Member States no discretion to impose stricter rules.

def: The bringing of national laws into closer alignment, short of complete uniformity.
ex: Article 114 TFEU is the principal legal basis for the approximation of laws.

def: The consolidation of an act and its amendments into a single new instrument without substantive change.
ex: The codification merged the original directive and its five amendments into one text.

def: A legislative technique combining substantive amendment with codification into a single new act.
ex: The recast repealed the earlier directive and introduced fresh obligations.

def: Interpreting a provision by reference to its purpose and objectives rather than its literal wording.
ex: The Court favoured a teleological reading that advanced the directive's aim.

def: Construing a text so as to give effect to its underlying purpose.
ex: A purposive interpretation prevailed over the literal wording of the provision.

def: The practice of imposing requirements beyond those a directive minimally demands when transposing it.
ex: Business groups complained of gold-plating in the national implementing regulations.

def: A negotiated exemption allowing a Member State not to participate in a particular Union policy.
ex: Denmark secured an opt-out from the single currency.

def: The extent to which a provision may be relied upon by individuals before the national courts.
ex: The directive's invocability against the state turned on its being unconditional and sufficiently precise.

def: The principle that national procedural rules for Union claims be no less favourable than those governing similar domestic claims.
ex: The remedy satisfied the requirement of equivalence but failed that of effectiveness.

def: The principle that national rules must not render the exercise of Union rights practically impossible or excessively difficult.
ex: The short limitation period offended the principle of effectiveness.

def: The private-international-law doctrine of referring back to another legal system's choice-of-law rules.
ex: The Regulation excludes renvoi, referring only to the substantive law it designates.

def: Transcending national authority, with powers exercised above the level of individual states.
ex: The Court of Justice is a genuinely supranational institution whose rulings bind the Member States.

def: The doctrine or practice of decision-making by institutions standing above the Member States.
ex: Supranationalism distinguishes the Union from a conventional international organisation.

def: A mode of cooperation in which the Member States retain control and decide by agreement among themselves.
ex: Foreign policy remains dominated by intergovernmentalism and the national veto.

def: The dynamic by which integration in one sector generates pressure to integrate in others.
ex: Neofunctionalists explained deepening integration through functional spillover.

def: The arrangement whereby Member States integrate at varying depths or speeds.
ex: Enhanced cooperation is a formal vehicle for differentiation among willing states.

def: Opposed to or critical of European integration.
ex: Eurosceptic members voted en bloc against ratification of the Treaty.

def: A supporter of European integration.
ex: The europhile majority pressed for deeper fiscal union.

def: An independent official who investigates complaints of maladministration against the Union institutions.
ex: The complainant referred the matter to the European Ombudsman.

def: A formal refusal to vote either for or against a proposal.
ex: A constructive abstention allowed the measure to pass without the dissenting state's support.

def: The office, rotating among the Member States, of chairing the Council of the European Union.
ex: The French presidency prioritised completion of the asylum reform.

def: The former name for the ordinary legislative procedure, in which the Parliament and the Council legislate jointly.
ex: Under co-decision, neither institution can adopt the act without the other.

def: The mechanism enabling a firm authorised in one Member State to provide services throughout the single market.
ex: Loss of passporting rights forced the bank to relocate its Union operations.

def: The self-standing character of the Union legal order, independent of both national and international law.
ex: The Court invoked the autonomy of Union law to reject the arbitration clause.

def: The authority conferred on the Union to act in a given field.
ex: The measure exceeded the Union's competence in the sphere of public health.

def: A party's legal entitlement to bring proceedings before a court.
ex: The applicant lacked standing, being neither directly nor individually concerned by the act.

def: Describing an act by which the Commission supplements or amends non-essential elements of a legislative act.
ex: The Parliament objected to the delegated act within the scrutiny period.

def: A court's willingness to defer to the assessments of the legislature or executive, affording them a margin of discretion.
ex: The Court showed marked deference to the legislature in complex economic matters.

def: The degree of certainty a party must reach to discharge its burden, whether the balance of probabilities in civil cases or beyond reasonable doubt in criminal ones.
ex: The judge reminded the jury that the criminal standard of proof is a demanding one and must not be diluted.

def: The civil standard of proof, satisfied where the tribunal is persuaded that a fact is more likely than not to be true.
ex: On the balance of probabilities, the court found that the defendant had signed the guarantee.

def: The obligation on a party to adduce sufficient evidence to raise an issue fit to be left to the tribunal, as distinct from the legal burden of persuading it.
ex: The defendant bore only an evidential burden in respect of self-defence, which then passed the persuasive burden back to the Crown.

def: The ultimate obligation to prove a fact in issue to the required standard, which never shifts during the course of a trial.
ex: Although the evidential burden may move between the parties, the legal burden of proving the contract remained on the claimant throughout.

def: To perform one's obligation to disclose documents by making and serving a list of the documents within one's control.
ex: The parties were ordered to give disclosure by exchanging lists within 28 days of the case management conference.

def: The default disclosure obligation requiring a party to disclose the documents on which it relies and those that adversely affect or support any party's case.
ex: The court dispensed with standard disclosure in favour of an issue-by-issue approach under the disclosure menu.

def: An order requiring a party to disclose particular documents or classes of document, or to carry out a further search, where standard disclosure is thought inadequate.
ex: The claimant applied for specific disclosure of the internal emails referred to in the defendant's own witness statement.

def: The rule protecting confidential communications between lawyer and client, and certain communications made for litigation, from compelled disclosure.
ex: Advice on the merits of the claim was covered by legal professional privilege and was properly redacted from the bundle.

def: The limb of legal professional privilege protecting confidential lawyer-client communications made for the purpose of giving or obtaining legal advice, whether or not litigation is contemplated.
ex: Because no litigation was in prospect, only legal advice privilege could be invoked over the compliance file.

def: To relinquish, expressly or by conduct, the protection that privilege would otherwise afford a document or communication.
ex: By deploying the advice in support of its defence, the company had waived privilege over the whole of the relevant file.

def: A formal notice served on the other party of an intention to rely on hearsay evidence, giving particulars of the statement and the reason the maker will not be called.
ex: The claimant served a hearsay notice in respect of the deceased surveyor's report so that it could be admitted at trial.

def: Describing evidence that the law excludes and which the tribunal may not take into account.
ex: Evidence of the defendant's previous convictions was ruled inadmissible as more prejudicial than probative.

def: The tendency of evidence to influence the tribunal unfairly, particularly by inviting reasoning that is not properly probative of the issue.
ex: The court excluded the material because its prejudicial effect substantially outweighed its probative value.

def: The logical relationship whereby evidence renders a fact in issue more or less probable, being the precondition of admissibility.
ex: Counsel challenged the relevance of the correspondence, arguing that it bore on no pleaded issue.

def: The persuasive value or cogency the tribunal attaches to admissible evidence when deciding the facts.
ex: Little weight could be given to the hearsay statement because the maker had not been available for cross-examination.

def: The further questioning of a witness by the party who called him, confined to matters arising out of cross-examination.
ex: In re-examination counsel repaired the apparent inconsistency by drawing out the context the earlier answer had omitted.

def: A question that suggests the desired answer or assumes a disputed fact, generally objectionable in examination-in-chief.
ex: Opposing counsel objected that the question was leading and invited the witness merely to agree.

def: A signed declaration verifying that the maker believes the facts stated in a document to be true, breach of which may expose the maker to proceedings for contempt of court.
ex: The particulars of claim were struck out because they were not supported by a valid statement of truth.

def: Opinion evidence given by a suitably qualified witness on matters calling for specialised knowledge outside the tribunal's own experience.
ex: Expert evidence on the standard of care was admitted from a consultant of the relevant speciality.

def: The governing principle of the Civil Procedure Rules requiring the court to deal with cases justly and at proportionate cost.
ex: The judge refused the adjournment as inconsistent with the overriding objective and the efficient use of court resources.

def: The active control by the court of the conduct and progress of litigation, including the giving of directions and the fixing of a timetable.
ex: At the case management conference the court allocated the claim to the multi-track and gave directions to trial.

def: Orders of the court regulating the steps the parties must take to prepare a case for trial, such as disclosure, exchange of statements and expert reports.
ex: The parties were unable to agree directions, so the court imposed a timetable of its own.

def: To order the deletion of a statement of case, in whole or in part, where it discloses no reasonable ground, is an abuse of process, or breaches a rule or order.
ex: The defence was struck out for repeated non-compliance with the court's unless order.

def: A judgment given without a full trial where the court is satisfied that a claim or defence has no real prospect of success and there is no other compelling reason for a trial.
ex: The claimant obtained summary judgment because the defence disclosed no arguable answer to the debt.

def: The statement of case setting out the facts on which the claimant relies and the remedy sought.
ex: The particulars of claim pleaded the misrepresentation with the specificity the rules require.

def: The document by which a party gives disclosure, identifying the documents within its control and stating any claim to withhold inspection.
ex: The second part of the list of documents itemised the material over which privilege was asserted.

def: The threshold, more than merely fanciful but not requiring probable success, that a claim or defence must meet to survive summary determination.
ex: Permission to defend was granted because the guarantor had a real prospect of establishing that the demand was invalid.

def: A statutory provision placing the legal burden of proving a particular matter on the defendant rather than on the prosecution.
ex: The court read down the reverse burden as merely evidential to render the provision compatible with the presumption of innocence.

def: Tending to cause unfair harm to a party, especially by outweighing an item's probative value.
ex: Evidence of the accused's prior convictions was ruled too prejudicial to go before the jury.

def: Of evidence, proving a fact indirectly by inference rather than by direct observation.
ex: The conviction rested entirely on circumstantial evidence, since no witness had seen the act itself.

def: Of evidence or argument, clear, logical and convincing.
ex: The tribunal found the expert's reasoning cogent and preferred it to the claimant's account.

def: The documented history of an item's origin and successive custody, bearing on its authenticity.
ex: Gaps in the painting's provenance cast serious doubt on the vendor's claim to good title.

def: To withdraw or formally retract a previous statement or item of testimony.
ex: The key witness later recanted, claiming his original statement had been made under pressure.

def: To dispute or contest the truth of an assertion.
ex: The defence did not seriously controvert the fact of the collision, only the question of fault.

def: To deny or contradict.
ex: There was no gainsaying the documentary record, which flatly contradicted the witness's recollection.

def: An inference that the law requires or permits to be drawn until it is displaced by contrary evidence.
ex: The presumption of innocence places the burden squarely on the prosecution throughout the trial.

def: Of a presumption, capable of being displaced by evidence to the contrary.
ex: Legitimacy is a rebuttable presumption that scientific testing can readily overturn.

def: A conclusion drawn by reasoning from facts already established.
ex: The jury were entitled to draw an adverse inference from the defendant's silence in interview.

def: The burden or obligation of proving a fact in issue.
ex: The onus lay on the party asserting fraud to prove it with cogent evidence.

def: The greater weight of the evidence, constituting the ordinary civil standard of proof.
ex: A civil claimant need only establish liability on the preponderance of the evidence.

def: A solemn non-religious declaration of truth made in place of an oath.
ex: The witness, having no religious belief, gave her evidence on affirmation rather than on oath.

def: A sworn statement confirming the truth of the contents of a pleading.
ex: Each statement of case must be supported by a verification signed by the party or its representative.

def: In old common-law pleading, the defendant's answer to the plaintiff's surrejoinder.
ex: The archaic sequence of replication, rejoinder, surrejoinder and rebutter has long since been abolished.

def: In old common-law pleading, the plaintiff's reply to the defendant's rebutter.
ex: The surrebutter was the plaintiff's final permitted pleading in the classical order of pleading.

def: Of a document or information, subject to compulsory disclosure to the opposing party.
ex: The tribunal held that internal risk assessments were discoverable and not shielded by privilege.

def: The barring of a party from relitigating a claim or issue already finally decided.
ex: Issue preclusion prevented the defendant from reopening a question of causation settled in the earlier action.

def: The postponement or adjournment of court proceedings to a later date.
ex: Defence counsel sought a continuance to secure the attendance of an essential expert witness.

def: The voluntary termination of a civil action by the party who brought it.
ex: Notice of discontinuance was served, though the claimant remained liable for the defendant's costs.

def: A formal notice entered to suspend a proceeding until the person lodging it has been heard.
ex: A caveat was lodged at the probate registry to prevent a grant issuing on the disputed will.

def: A third party holding money owed to a debtor who is ordered by the court to pay it to the creditor.
ex: The bank, as garnishee, was directed to pay the frozen funds directly to the judgment creditor.

def: To enforce the forfeiture of a recognizance or bail bond.
ex: When the accused absconded, the court moved to estreat the surety's recognizance.

def: The sending of a defendant to a higher court for trial, or of a person to prison, by court order.
ex: The magistrates ordered committal for trial once satisfied there was a case to answer.

def: An expense paid out by a solicitor on the client's behalf and recoverable as part of the costs.
ex: The bill of costs distinguished the solicitor's fees from disbursements such as court fees and counsel's brief.

def: A court's list or register of the cases and proceedings before it.
ex: The motion languished on a congested docket for the better part of a year.

def: A judicial officer who deals with the procedural and administrative conduct of proceedings.
ex: Interlocutory applications were heard by the registrar rather than by the trial judge.

def: An officer who executes court orders such as seizures, evictions and the enforcement of judgments.
ex: The bailiff attended the premises to levy execution on goods to satisfy the judgment.

def: A bystander summoned to serve on a jury when the regular panel is deficient in number.
ex: When two jurors fell ill, the sheriff summoned a talesman from among those present in the court.

def: The improper joining of parties or causes of action in a single proceeding.
ex: The defendant applied to sever the claims, alleging misjoinder of unrelated causes of action.

def: The failure to join a party who ought to have been included in the proceedings.
ex: The action was stayed for nonjoinder of a co-owner whose interest could not be determined in his absence.

def: The suspension or termination of legal proceedings, as on the death of a party.
ex: The claimant's death worked an abatement of the suit until his personal representatives were substituted.

def: A provisional court order stating that a couple is entitled to divorce but which does not yet dissolve the marriage.
ex: The judge pronounced the decree nisi in open court, and the parties were told they could apply for the final decree six weeks later.

def: The final court order that legally ends a marriage and leaves both parties free to remarry.
ex: We advised the client not to remarry until the decree absolute had been sealed by the court.

def: The spouse who starts divorce proceedings by filing the initial application.
ex: As the petitioner, your wife will be the party who issues the divorce application.

def: The sole legal ground for divorce, meaning the marriage has broken down beyond any prospect of reconciliation.
ex: Under the current law, the applicant need only confirm the irretrievable breakdown of the marriage.

def: The property in which a married couple lived together as their main residence.
ex: The dispute centred on whether the wife could remain in the matrimonial home until the youngest child turned eighteen.

def: The agreement or court order dividing a couple's assets, income and liabilities on divorce.
ex: Both parties reached a financial settlement that gave the wife a larger share of the equity in return for a clean break.

def: A financial arrangement that ends all ongoing financial obligations between spouses so neither can make future claims against the other.
ex: Our client wanted a clean break so that his ex-wife could not return to court for maintenance years later.

def: A court order that gives legal effect to a financial agreement the parties have reached themselves.
ex: Once both spouses signed the agreement, we drafted a consent order for the judge to approve.

def: Regular payments made by one spouse to support the other after divorce or separation.
ex: The court ordered spousal maintenance of £1,500 per month for a period of five years.

def: Financial support paid by a parent towards the everyday costs of raising their child.
ex: Child maintenance was assessed by the Child Maintenance Service based on the father's gross weekly income.

def: Regular sums payable under a court order, typically as ongoing maintenance for a spouse or child.
ex: The order provided for periodical payments to continue until the wife remarried or either party died.

def: A court order requiring one party to pay the other a single fixed sum of money.
ex: In place of ongoing maintenance, the husband agreed to a lump sum order of £200,000 to achieve a clean break.

def: A court order that transfers a percentage of one spouse's pension into a pension arrangement for the other.
ex: The wife obtained a pension sharing order giving her forty per cent of her husband's occupational pension.

def: The property and financial resources built up by a couple during their marriage that are available for division on divorce.
ex: The family home and the joint savings were treated as matrimonial assets to be shared equally.

def: Assets acquired before the marriage or received by inheritance or gift, which may be excluded from the division of assets.
ex: The inheritance he received from his late father was argued to be non-matrimonial property and ring-fenced from the settlement.

def: To protect an asset from division by treating it as separate from the shared marital pot.
ex: We sought to ring-fence the business, arguing it had been established long before the marriage.

def: The obligation on each party to provide full and honest information about their assets, income and liabilities.
ex: The wife's solicitor accused the husband of incomplete financial disclosure and demanded copies of his overseas bank statements.

def: The standard court document in which each party sets out their full financial circumstances in contested financial proceedings.
ex: We spent the afternoon completing the client's Form E and gathering the supporting valuations.

def: The duty to reveal all relevant financial information openly and without concealment.
ex: The judge set aside the order after finding that the husband had failed to give full and frank disclosure of an offshore trust.

def: The legal rights, duties and authority a parent has in relation to a child and the child's property.
ex: As the father was not married to the mother, he acquired parental responsibility only when he was named on the birth certificate.

def: A court order settling with whom a child is to live and how much time they spend with each parent.
ex: The court made a child arrangements order providing that the children live with their mother and stay with their father every other weekend.

def: The arrangement determining which parent a child lives with on a day-to-day basis.
ex: The mother was granted primary residence, with the father having generous contact.

def: The time a child spends or communicates with the parent they do not live with.
ex: The father applied to court after the mother repeatedly refused him contact with the children.

def: An arrangement under which a child divides their time substantially between both parents' homes.
ex: The parents agreed a shared care arrangement of week-on, week-off during term time.

def: The child's overall wellbeing, which the court treats as its paramount consideration in any decision about the child.
ex: The judge stressed that the welfare of the child was paramount and outweighed the father's own wishes.

def: The overriding factor that must take priority above all others, namely the child's welfare in family proceedings.
ex: In deciding residence, the child's welfare is the paramount consideration for the court.

def: The statutory list of factors the court must weigh when deciding what is in a child's best interests.
ex: Counsel took the judge through each item on the welfare checklist, from the child's wishes to any risk of harm.

def: The standard by which a court decides what outcome will most benefit a child's welfare and development.
ex: It was plainly in the children's best interests to remain in the same school throughout the proceedings.

def: A court order preventing a parent from taking a specified action concerning a child without the court's consent.
ex: We obtained a prohibited steps order to stop the father removing the child from the jurisdiction.

def: A court order that decides a particular question about how a child is to be brought up.
ex: The mother applied for a specific issue order to allow the child to be enrolled at a faith school.

def: A person legally appointed to take responsibility for a child, usually where the parents are unable to do so.
ex: The will named the children's aunt as their testamentary guardian in the event of both parents' death.

def: The legal responsibility and authority a guardian holds over a child's care and upbringing.
ex: On the death of both parents, guardianship of the infant passed to her grandmother.

def: An independent officer appointed to represent a child's interests in certain family court proceedings.
ex: The children's guardian filed a report recommending that the child remain in foster care pending assessment.

def: The body that advises the family courts about the welfare of children and what arrangements are safe and in their best interests.
ex: The Cafcass officer interviewed both parents before preparing a section 7 report for the court.

def: A welfare report prepared for the court on the circumstances of a child in a dispute about their arrangements.
ex: The judge adjourned the hearing until the section 7 report had been filed and served on both parties.

def: A court order protecting a person from being harassed, threatened or subjected to violence by an associated person.
ex: We secured a non-molestation order the same day, forbidding the former partner from contacting our client.

def: A court order regulating who may live in the family home and on what terms.
ex: The judge granted an occupation order excluding the abusive husband from the property for six months.

def: Controlling, coercive, threatening, violent or abusive behaviour between people who are or have been in a relationship.
ex: Allegations of domestic abuse meant the court had to consider whether contact could take place safely.

def: A pattern of controlling and intimidating behaviour used by one partner to dominate the other.
ex: The wife's statement described sustained coercive control over the family finances throughout the marriage.

def: An agreement made before marriage setting out how the couple's assets are to be divided if they later divorce.
ex: Both parties took independent legal advice before signing the prenuptial agreement.

def: An agreement made after marriage regulating how assets will be divided in the event of a future divorce.
ex: After the inheritance came through, the couple entered into a postnuptial agreement to protect those funds.

def: A divorce granted without either party having to prove wrongdoing by the other.
ex: Since the introduction of no-fault divorce, neither spouse needs to allege adultery or unreasonable behaviour.

def: The legal process of formally ending a civil partnership, equivalent to divorce for married couples.
ex: The couple applied for dissolution of their civil partnership after two years of separation.

def: To formally begin divorce proceedings by submitting an application to the court.
ex: She decided to file for divorce once it was clear the marriage could not be saved.

def: The form by which the respondent confirms they have received the divorce application.
ex: The divorce could not progress until the respondent returned the acknowledgement of service.

def: A party's behaviour during the marriage which, if serious enough, the court may take into account when dividing assets.
ex: The husband's dissipation of assets amounted to conduct the court could not ignore in the settlement.

def: A method of dividing assets on divorce focused on meeting each party's reasonable housing and income requirements.
ex: Given the modest assets, the court adopted a needs-based approach to ensure both parties could be rehoused.

def: The court proceedings and orders through which financial matters are resolved on divorce.
ex: When negotiations broke down, the wife issued financial remedy proceedings to have the assets divided by the court.

def: A foundational document subscribed by a company's first members stating their intention to form it.
ex: Each subscriber signed the memorandum, agreeing to take at least one share in the new company.

def: To formally call together and open a meeting.
ex: The chairman convened an extraordinary general meeting to consider the rescue proposal.

def: To suspend a meeting with the intention of resuming it later.
ex: The meeting was adjourned for two weeks so that the auditors could complete their report.

def: To assemble a meeting again after an adjournment.
ex: The board reconvened the following morning to finalise the terms of the acquisition.

def: To decline to cast a vote either for or against a resolution.
ex: Two directors abstained from voting because of their personal interest in the transaction.

def: The largest number of votes cast for one option, though short of an overall majority.
ex: The candidate was elected to the board on a plurality, having secured more votes than any rival.

def: Full, complete, and unqualified, especially of powers or an assembly.
ex: The general meeting exercised its plenary authority to overturn the board's decision.

def: Designating an additional deciding vote given to the chair when the votes are equally divided.
ex: The chairman used his casting vote to break the deadlock on the board.

def: A vote taken by counting the shares held by each member rather than by a show of hands.
ex: A poll was demanded so that the votes of the major shareholders would be properly weighted.

def: A complete standstill in decision-making caused by an even division of votes or interests.
ex: The equal shareholding produced a deadlock that could only be resolved by winding up the company.

def: The authority conferred on directors or agents to act on the company's behalf.
ex: The board exceeded its mandate by committing the company to an unrelated venture.

def: The total pay and benefits received by a director or employee for their services.
ex: The remuneration committee set the executives' pay by reference to comparable listed companies.

def: A salary, fee, or other profit derived from holding an office or employment.
ex: The report disclosed every emolument paid to the directors during the financial year.

def: The responsible oversight and safeguarding of a company's affairs on behalf of others.
ex: Institutional investors are expected to exercise active stewardship over the companies they own.

def: The obligation of directors to answer for their conduct and decisions to the members.
ex: The governance code strengthens the accountability of the board to shareholders.

def: Complete integrity and honesty in the conduct of an office.
ex: A director's probity was called into question after the undisclosed related-party dealings emerged.

def: Supervisory monitoring of a company's management and internal controls.
ex: The audit committee provides independent oversight of the company's financial reporting.

def: An independent professional appointed to examine and report on a company's accounts.
ex: The auditor qualified the accounts, warning that the going-concern basis was in doubt.

def: A person who agrees in the founding documents to take shares in a company.
ex: The original subscribers to the memorandum became the company's first members.

def: A provisional certificate entitling the holder to shares, often issued in lieu of a cash dividend.
ex: The company offered a scrip dividend, allowing shareholders to take new shares instead of cash.

def: Relating to the enjoyment of the real benefit of shares, as distinct from the bare legal title.
ex: The nominee held the legal title while the fund remained the beneficial owner of the shares.

def: To deprive a shareholder of the right to vote.
ex: Failure to disclose the interest disenfranchised the holder in respect of the relevant shares.

def: To confer voting rights on a class of shareholders.
ex: The reorganisation enfranchised the previously non-voting shares.

def: To remove a company's securities from trading on a stock exchange.
ex: The board resolved to delist the shares and take the company private.

def: The disposal of a subsidiary, business unit, or holding.
ex: The divestment of the non-core assets raised sufficient capital to reduce the group's borrowings.

def: To reform a board or body with a fresh composition.
ex: Following the resignations, the board was reconstituted with a majority of independent directors.

def: To combine two or more companies into a single entity.
ex: The two rivals agreed to amalgamate their businesses under a new holding company.

def: To convert profits or reserves into share capital, or to provide a company with capital.
ex: The directors resolved to capitalise the reserves by issuing bonus shares to the members.

def: A company connected to another through common ownership or control.
ex: The loan was made to an overseas affiliate within the same corporate group.

def: Describing profits lawfully available to be paid out as a dividend.
ex: A dividend may be paid only out of the company's distributable reserves.

def: The state of being able to meet debts as they fall due.
ex: The directors signed a statement of solvency before the capital reduction proceeded.

def: Characterised by unlawful, unjust, or improper conduct, as in a director's trading on with no reasonable prospect of avoiding insolvency.
ex: The liquidator alleged wrongful trading against the directors who had traded on while hopelessly insolvent.

def: Capable of being entrusted to another to perform.
ex: Certain statutory duties of the board are not delegable to a committee.

def: Describing a director who supervises but takes no part in day-to-day management.
ex: The board appointed two non-executive directors to strengthen its independent oversight.

def: A person or group with a legitimate interest in a company's conduct beyond its shareholders.
ex: The revised duty requires directors to have regard to the interests of employees and other stakeholders.

def: Concerned with the careful discussion and weighing of matters before a decision.
ex: The board acts as a deliberative body, debating strategy before resolving upon it.

def: A system in which employees share in company decision-making through board representation.
ex: German codetermination gives workers seats on the supervisory board of large companies.

def: Describing a voting or dividend right that accumulates rather than lapsing if unused.
ex: Cumulative voting allowed the minority to concentrate their votes and elect one director.

def: Describing shares that the company may or must buy back on stated terms.
ex: The redeemable preference shares were bought back at par on the agreed date.

def: Describing securities that may be exchanged for shares of another class.
ex: The convertible loan notes were later converted into ordinary shares.

def: The passing of shares by operation of law, as on the holder's death or bankruptcy.
ex: On the shareholder's death, transmission of the shares vested them in his personal representatives.

def: To fix provisions in the articles so that they can be altered only by an enhanced procedure.
ex: The founders sought to entrench their veto rights against later amendment.

def: The right to vote conferred by membership of a company.
ex: The reclassification extended the franchise to the holders of the deferred shares.

def: The holding of an office or position, or the period during which it is held.
ex: Several major acquisitions were completed during the chairman's incumbency.

def: The term or conditions under which an office is held.
ex: The governance code recommends that a director's tenure should not exceed nine years.

def: Describing a right that may never be suspended, even during a public emergency.
ex: The prohibition of torture is non-derogable and admits of no exception.

def: Incapable of being taken away, surrendered or transferred.
ex: The declaration proclaims the inalienable rights of every human being.

def: The principle that civil, political, economic and social rights form a single inseparable whole.
ex: The conference reaffirmed the indivisibility of all human rights.

def: The principle that human rights belong to everyone everywhere, irrespective of culture or status.
ex: Critics argue that universality masks a Western conception of rights.

def: The return of a person to a country where they face persecution or serious harm.
ex: Deporting the applicant would amount to refoulement in breach of the Convention.

def: The principle prohibiting the return of a person to a place where they risk persecution or torture.
ex: The principle of non-refoulement barred her removal to the requesting state.

def: The extension of a state's human-rights obligations to acts committed outside its own borders.
ex: The claimants relied on extraterritoriality to hold the armed forces accountable abroad.

def: Redress owed to a victim for a violation, encompassing compensation, restitution and rehabilitation.
ex: The tribunal ordered full reparation for the victims of the atrocities.

def: The remedying of a wrong, or the means by which a wrong is set right.
ex: Victims of the abuse were left without any effective redress.

def: Exemption from punishment or accountability for human-rights violations.
ex: The blanket amnesty entrenched a culture of impunity for state killings.

def: Acts committed with intent to destroy, in whole or in part, a national, ethnic, racial or religious group.
ex: The court found that the massacres amounted to genocide.

def: Serious and systematic ill-treatment of a person on account of their identity or beliefs.
ex: She was granted asylum after establishing a well-founded fear of persecution.

def: The formal removal of a foreign national from a state's territory.
ex: The deportation was halted because of the real risk of torture on return.

def: The compulsory removal of a person or group from a country.
ex: The collective expulsion of the migrants breached the Convention.

def: The transfer of a person to another state, often outside lawful extradition, for interrogation or detention.
ex: The inquiry exposed the state's complicity in extraordinary rendition.

def: Held in detention without any contact with the outside world.
ex: He was held incommunicado for weeks, with no access to a lawyer.

def: Based on individual discretion rather than law, and therefore unjust or unpredictable.
ex: The tribunal condemned his arbitrary detention without charge or trial.

def: An institutionalised regime of systematic oppression and domination by one racial group over another.
ex: The crime of apartheid is now recognised as a crime against humanity.

def: The deprivation of a person's right to vote.
ex: The blanket disenfranchisement of prisoners was held incompatible with the Convention.

def: The right to vote in political elections.
ex: Universal suffrage was secured only after decades of struggle.

def: The protection granted by a state to someone fleeing persecution in another country.
ex: She sought asylum on the ground of political persecution.

def: The condition of not being recognised as a national by any state under the operation of its law.
ex: The withdrawal of citizenship plunged thousands into statelessness.

def: The legal process by which a foreign national acquires the citizenship of a state.
ex: His naturalisation was revoked on national-security grounds.

def: The return of a person to their country of nationality or origin.
ex: The voluntary repatriation of the refugees required firm security guarantees.

def: The recruitment or transport of people through coercion or deception for the purpose of exploitation.
ex: The victims of trafficking were wrongly treated as offenders rather than as victims.

def: A condition in which a person is compelled to live and work under another's control, without the ability to leave.
ex: The Convention prohibits slavery, servitude and forced labour.

def: The exercise of any or all of the powers attaching to the right of ownership over a person.
ex: Enslavement is enumerated among the crimes against humanity.

def: Compulsory enlistment of persons into military service.
ex: The forced conscription of children constitutes a grave violation of international law.

def: A unilateral statement by which a state excludes or modifies the legal effect of certain treaty provisions.
ex: Several states entered a reservation to the article on freedom of religion.

def: A state that has signed a treaty.
ex: As a signatory, the state was bound to refrain from defeating the treaty's object and purpose.

def: The right of a people to freely determine their political status and pursue their economic, social and cultural development.
ex: The territory invoked its right to self-determination.

def: The principle that the International Criminal Court acts only where national courts are unwilling or unable genuinely to prosecute.
ex: Under complementarity, the Court deferred to the ongoing national trial.

def: Retaliatory action taken against a person for cooperating with human-rights bodies or reporting abuses.
ex: The witnesses feared reprisals for testifying before the commission.

def: Causing physical or mental suffering of a severity that offends human dignity.
ex: The conditions of detention amounted to inhuman treatment.

def: Humiliating a person or diminishing their dignity to a serious degree.
ex: Strip-searching the detainees in public was found to be degrading treatment.

def: Occurring outside the authority or process of a court of law.
ex: The report documented a pattern of extrajudicial killings by the security forces.

def: The abduction of a person by the state followed by a refusal to acknowledge their detention or fate.
ex: Enforced disappearance places the victim outside the protection of the law.

def: The extent to which human-rights obligations bind private parties as well as the state.
ex: The doctrine of horizontality allowed the right to be invoked against a private employer.

def: The systematic monitoring of persons, often engaging the right to respect for private life.
ex: The bulk surveillance programme was held to violate the right to privacy.

def: The suppression or restriction of expression by a public authority.
ex: State censorship of the press stifled all political dissent.

def: Speech or conduct treated as insulting to religion, the criminalisation of which may restrict free expression.
ex: Human-rights bodies have urged the repeal of blasphemy laws.

def: The integration of a human-rights perspective into all policies, programmes and institutions.
ex: Gender mainstreaming became central to the agency's work.

def: The mutual reliance of different categories of rights, each reinforcing the others.
ex: The Vienna Declaration stressed the interdependence of all human rights.

def: A heightened exposure to harm that may warrant special legal protection.
ex: The court took account of the applicant's particular vulnerability as an unaccompanied minor.

def: The process of pushing a group to the edges of society and denying it full participation.
ex: The policy deepened the marginalisation of the indigenous community.

def: The process of enabling people to assert and exercise their rights.
ex: The programme focused on the legal empowerment of rural women.

def: The principle that rights must be secured without distinction on prohibited grounds such as race, sex or religion.
ex: The principle of non-discrimination underpins the entire Convention.

def: A person who has already been granted asylum, as distinct from a pending asylum-seeker.
ex: As a recognised asylee, he became eligible to apply for permanent residence one year after the grant.

def: A person who is being, or has been, deported from a country.
ex: The charter flight carried thirty deportees back to their country of origin under escort.

def: The legal condition of being liable to removal or deportation from a state.
ex: Counsel conceded removability but sought relief in the form of cancellation of removal.

def: The status of a foreign national who is barred by law from being admitted to or remaining in a country.
ex: A prior misrepresentation triggered a ground of inadmissibility that only a waiver could overcome.

def: The revocation of a person's acquired citizenship, usually for fraud in the naturalisation process or on public-interest grounds.
ex: The government initiated denaturalisation proceedings after discovering he had concealed his wartime conduct.

def: A person who remains in a country beyond the period permitted by their visa or leave.
ex: Once his student visa expired, he became an overstayer and lost the right to work.

def: The formal undertaking by a person or employer to support a foreign national's application to enter or remain.
ex: Her work visa depended on continued sponsorship by a licensed employer.

def: The foreign national on whose behalf an immigration petition or application is made.
ex: The beneficiary of the visa petition was required to attend a consular interview abroad.

def: A person held in immigration custody pending a decision on their status or removal.
ex: The detainee applied for bail after spending four months in the removal centre.

def: A foreign national permitted to enter or remain temporarily on humanitarian or public-interest grounds without a formal admission.
ex: As a humanitarian parolee, she was allowed to remain while her sponsor's petition was adjudicated.

def: An official who hears and determines immigration claims or appeals.
ex: The adjudicator dismissed the appeal, finding the applicant's account lacking in credibility.

def: Measurable physical identifiers, such as fingerprints and facial images, collected to verify a person's identity.
ex: Applicants must enrol their biometrics before a residence permit can be issued.

def: The country a person treats as their permanent home and to which they intend to return.
ex: His domicile of origin remained abroad despite decades of residence in the United Kingdom.

def: Historically, a foreign national granted certain rights of a subject short of full citizenship; more broadly, a lawful inhabitant.
ex: By letters patent the alien was made a denizen, acquiring the right to hold land.

def: A person residing in a country temporarily rather than permanently.
ex: As a mere sojourner on a visitor visa, he had no recourse to public funds.

def: Liable in law to be refused admission to a country at the border.
ex: On the basis of the fraud finding, the traveller was held to be excludable and refused entry.

def: The formal cancellation of a visa, permit or grant of status previously issued.
ex: The revocation of his sponsor licence left dozens of workers without valid leave.

def: A person who has failed to comply with immigration conditions and cannot be traced by the authorities.
ex: Classified as an absconder, she had a fresh removal order issued once located.

def: A form of discretionary relief that halts removal and confers or restores lawful status.
ex: He sought cancellation of removal on the basis of exceptional hardship to his citizen children.

def: Depending on the judgment of a decision-maker rather than arising as of right.
ex: Leave outside the Rules is a discretionary grant that the Secretary of State may refuse.

def: A general measure regularising the status of a class of unlawfully present migrants.
ex: The proposed amnesty would have allowed long-resident undocumented workers to regularise their position.

def: The process by which an unlawfully present migrant obtains lawful immigration status.
ex: The scheme offered regularisation to those who could prove ten years' continuous residence.

def: The shortening of a period of leave so that it expires earlier than originally granted.
ex: Withdrawal of sponsorship led to curtailment of his leave, giving him sixty days to find a new employer.

def: To cut short a person's existing period of leave to enter or remain.
ex: The Home Office may curtail leave where the holder ceases to meet the conditions of the visa.

def: Officially forbidden or banned, especially of an organisation whose membership bars a person from admission.
ex: His affiliation with a proscribed organisation rendered him inadmissible on security grounds.

def: Liable to be deported by reason of unlawful status or a specified ground.
ex: His conviction rendered him a deportable non-citizen despite his long residence.

def: The ending of refugee status where the circumstances giving rise to it have ceased to exist.
ex: The authorities invoked the cessation clause after conditions in his home country fundamentally changed.

def: The state of lacking the means to meet essential living needs, often relevant to support entitlements.
ex: Barred from working and from public funds, the family faced imminent destitution.

def: The loyalty owed by a person to the state of which they are a national or subject.
ex: The naturalisation ceremony required him to pledge his allegiance to the Crown.

def: To renounce solemnly, as of a prior allegiance upon naturalisation.
ex: The oath required the applicant to abjure all foreign allegiances upon becoming a citizen.

def: Not recognised as a national by any state under the operation of its law.
ex: Rendered stateless by the withdrawal of his citizenship, he could not lawfully be removed anywhere.

def: Present in a country without the authorisation or papers required by immigration law.
ex: Undocumented workers are especially vulnerable to exploitation by unscrupulous employers.

def: Carried out secretly, as of unlawful entry concealed from border authorities.
ex: He made a clandestine entry concealed in a lorry, evading immigration control altogether.

def: A family member who relies on a principal applicant and derives immigration status from them.
ex: Her spouse and children were admitted as dependants on her skilled-worker visa.

def: Relating to a consulate or the functions of a consul, especially the issuing of visas abroad.
ex: The visa was refused at the consular interview for want of proof of genuine intent.

def: The court-sanctioned imposition of a restructuring plan on a dissenting class of creditors that has voted against it.
ex: The senior lenders relied on the cram-down power to bind the junior noteholders who had rejected the scheme.

def: The prescribed order of priority in which realised funds are applied to different classes of claimant in an insolvency.
ex: Under the statutory waterfall, fixed-charge holders were paid before the preferential and unsecured creditors.

def: Describing a company, asset or debt whose value is impaired by financial difficulty or a heightened risk of default.
ex: The fund specialises in acquiring distressed debt at deep discounts to face value.

def: Having insufficient capital to meet the ordinary demands of a business or to absorb foreseeable losses.
ex: The subsidiary was chronically undercapitalised, leaving it unable to withstand a modest downturn.

def: The officeholder appointed to conduct the winding-up of a company, realise its assets and distribute the proceeds.
ex: The liquidator disclaimed the onerous lease and investigated the directors' pre-insolvency conduct.

def: An insolvency practitioner appointed to manage a company in administration and act in the interests of its creditors as a whole.
ex: The administrator continued trading the business while marketing it for sale as a going concern.

def: The shortfall remaining owed to a creditor after the realisation of security or distribution of assets.
ex: Following the sale, the lender proved for the deficiency as an unsecured creditor.

def: An agreement between a debtor and creditors under which the creditors accept partial payment in full settlement of their claims.
ex: The creditors approved a composition of sixty pence in the pound, avoiding a costly liquidation.

def: A formal agreement or protocol coordinating the conduct of parallel insolvency proceedings, especially across jurisdictions.
ex: The office-holders in each country negotiated a concordat to govern the cross-border realisation of assets.

def: The setting aside of a transaction entered into before insolvency, such as a preference or transaction at an undervalue.
ex: The office-holder brought avoidance proceedings to reverse the antecedent transfer of the warehouse.

def: A consensual, out-of-court restructuring of a distressed borrower's obligations negotiated with its creditors.
ex: The parties preferred a consensual workout to the cost and stigma of formal proceedings.

def: The process of restoring a financially distressed business to viability and profitability.
ex: A specialist was engaged to lead the turnaround before the liquidity crisis became terminal.

def: The reduction of a company's debt burden relative to its equity or assets.
ex: Aggressive deleveraging through asset sales averted a covenant default.

def: The legal seizure or freezing of a debtor's property to secure or satisfy a creditor's claim.
ex: The creditor obtained an attachment over the funds held in the debtor's account.

def: The mixing of trust or client money with a party's own funds so that the distinct assets become indistinguishable.
ex: The commingling of client monies with the firm's account complicated the tracing exercise.

def: The insolvency practitioner responsible for implementing and monitoring a voluntary arrangement.
ex: As supervisor of the arrangement, she collected contributions and paid the agreed dividends.

def: The insolvency practitioner who reviews a proposed voluntary arrangement and reports on it before creditors vote.
ex: The nominee concluded that the proposal had a reasonable prospect of being approved and implemented.

def: Describing a claim whose amount has not yet been fixed or agreed and must be quantified.
ex: The tort claim was admitted for voting purposes at an estimated value because it was unliquidated.

def: A liquidator's statutory power to renounce onerous property or unprofitable contracts, terminating the estate's rights and liabilities in them.
ex: The disclaimer of the leasehold released the estate from years of accruing rent.

def: Describing debt that ranks behind other obligations for repayment in the event of default or insolvency.
ex: Holders of the subordinated notes recovered nothing once the senior lenders had been paid.

def: Describing a category of unsecured claim, such as certain employee entitlements, that ranks ahead of ordinary creditors.
ex: The employees' unpaid wages were treated as preferential and paid before the general body of creditors.

def: The category of intangible legal rights protecting creations of the mind such as inventions, brands and creative works.
ex: The company's most valuable asset is its intellectual property, not its factories.

def: An exclusive right granted for an invention that is new, involves an inventive step and is capable of industrial application.
ex: The patent gives the pharmaceutical company a twenty-year monopoly on the drug.

def: To formally submit a request to a patent office seeking protection for an invention.
ex: We advised the client to file a patent application before disclosing the invention at the trade fair.

def: All information made public before a patent's filing date that is relevant to assessing the novelty of the invention.
ex: The examiner cited an obscure Japanese patent as prior art that anticipated our client's claims.

def: The requirement that an invention not be obvious to a person skilled in the relevant field.
ex: The opposition argued the modification lacked an inventive step and was obvious over the prior art.

def: The requirement that an invention has not been made available to the public anywhere before the filing date.
ex: Publishing the paper a week too early destroyed the novelty of the invention.

def: The numbered statement in a patent that legally defines the scope of the protection sought.
ex: Claim 1 was drafted too broadly and was held invalid for lack of novelty.

def: The full written description of an invention filed with the claims, enabling a skilled person to reproduce it.
ex: The specification must disclose the best method of performing the invention.

def: The point at which a patent office officially confers patent rights on the applicant.
ex: Enforcement rights arise only on grant of the patent, not on filing.

def: The date from which the novelty and inventive step of an application are assessed, usually the first filing date.
ex: The later application claimed the priority date of the earlier UK filing.

def: A notice indicating that a patent application has been filed but not yet granted.
ex: The product was marked 'patent pending' to deter would-be copyists.

def: A sign capable of distinguishing the goods or services of one undertaking from those of others.
ex: Their trade mark is one of the most recognisable logos in the world.

def: To record a mark on an official register so as to obtain statutory protection for it.
ex: We advised the start-up to register the trade mark in all its key export markets.

def: The quality of a mark that enables consumers to identify the commercial origin of goods or services.
ex: The application was refused because the word 'Fresh' lacked distinctive character for fruit juice.

def: A mark that merely describes a characteristic of the goods and is therefore generally unregistrable.
ex: 'Cold and Creamy' was rejected as a descriptive mark for ice cream.

def: The risk that the public would mistakenly believe that goods bearing similar marks come from the same source.
ex: The court found a likelihood of confusion between the two beverage brands.

def: The right protecting original literary, artistic, musical and other works against unauthorised copying.
ex: Copyright in the software vests in the employer, not the individual programmer.

def: The state of copyright automatically existing in a qualifying original work without any registration.
ex: Copyright subsists in the photographs from the moment they were taken.

def: A work that originates from its author and involves the author's own intellectual creation rather than copying.
ex: Only an original work attracts copyright, so a slavish reproduction is not protected.

def: The author's personal rights to be identified as creator and to object to derogatory treatment of the work.
ex: The author asserted her moral rights and objected to the mutilated adaptation.

def: A limited defence permitting certain uses of a copyright work, such as for criticism, review or news reporting.
ex: The quotation fell within fair dealing for the purpose of criticism.

def: To do an act that falls within the exclusive rights of an intellectual property owner without permission.
ex: The generic manufacturer was found to infringe the process patent.

def: A formal letter demanding that the recipient stop an allegedly infringing activity and refrain from repeating it.
ex: Our first step was to send a cease and desist letter to the online seller.

def: A temporary court order granted before trial to preserve the position until the dispute is finally decided.
ex: We applied for an interim injunction to halt the product launch pending trial.

def: A permission granted by a rights holder allowing another to use the intellectual property on agreed terms.
ex: The software is supplied under a licence rather than sold outright.

def: To confer permission on another party to exploit an intellectual property right.
ex: The university agreed to grant a licence to the spin-out company to commercialise the technology.

def: A licence under which only the licensee may exploit the right, to the exclusion even of the owner.
ex: Under the exclusive licence, not even the patentee could work the invention in that territory.

def: A licence that allows the owner to grant the same rights to other licensees as well.
ex: The photographer offered a non-exclusive licence so the image could be sold repeatedly.

def: Describing a licence for which no ongoing per-use or per-sale payment is required.
ex: The client wanted a perpetual, royalty-free licence to use the code.

def: To transfer ownership of an intellectual property right to another person.
ex: The founder agreed to assign all background IP to the company on incorporation.

def: Confidential business information that derives commercial value from being kept secret.
ex: The recipe is protected as a trade secret rather than by patent.

def: Information imparted in circumstances importing an obligation of confidence and not in the public domain.
ex: The departing employee misused confidential information to solicit clients.

def: A contract by which parties agree to keep specified information confidential.
ex: No technical details were shared until the non-disclosure agreement had been signed.

def: A right protecting the appearance of a product, such as its shape, contours or ornamentation.
ex: The distinctive bottle shape was protected as a registered design.

def: Goods bearing a mark identical to a registered trade mark without authorisation, designed to deceive.
ex: Customs seized a container of counterfeit goods bearing our client's logo.

def: The principle that an IP owner's control over a particular item ends once it has been lawfully sold.
ex: The parallel importer relied on exhaustion of rights to resell goods first sold within the EEA.

def: Genuine branded goods imported and sold in a market without the rights holder's consent, exploiting price differences.
ex: The brand owner sought to block parallel imports from outside the EEA.

def: To cancel a granted patent, typically on the ground that it should never have been granted.
ex: The court agreed to revoke the patent for lack of inventive step.

def: A procedure allowing third parties to challenge a patent or trade mark at the relevant office after or before grant.
ex: A competitor filed opposition proceedings against our client's European patent.

def: The ability to commercialise a product without infringing the intellectual property rights of others.
ex: Before launch, we conducted a freedom to operate analysis on the third-party patents.

def: A mark with such a strong reputation that it enjoys protection beyond the goods for which it is registered.
ex: As a well-known mark, it was protected even against use on unrelated products.

def: The party who grants a licence to use an intellectual property right.
ex: As licensor, the studio retained the right to audit the distributor's sales.

def: The party who receives permission to use an intellectual property right under a licence.
ex: The licensee was obliged to report quarterly sales to calculate the royalty due.

def: The quality of satisfying the statutory conditions for a valid patent, chiefly novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability.
ex: Counsel challenged the patentability of the algorithm, arguing it was an excluded mathematical method.

def: The ground of invalidity that an invention would have been obvious to a skilled person in light of the prior art.
ex: The patent was revoked for obviousness, the modification being a routine workshop variation.

def: The disclosure of every feature of an invention by a single earlier item of prior art, thereby depriving it of novelty.
ex: An enabling anticipation in the earlier journal article rendered claim one invalid.

def: The presence of an inventive step distinguishing an invention from the obvious development of existing knowledge.
ex: The tribunal accepted that combining the two known elements involved genuine inventiveness.

def: The document filed with a patent application that describes the invention and sets out the claims defining its scope.
ex: The examiner objected that the specification did not support the breadth of the claims.

def: A particular form or worked example in which a claimed invention is put into practice.
ex: The preferred embodiment described in the patent used a titanium housing.

def: A later application carved out of an earlier one, retaining its filing date but claiming distinct subject matter.
ex: The applicant filed a divisional to pursue the second invention the examiner had objected to.

def: The process of pursuing an application through examination and correspondence until grant or refusal.
ex: Statements made during prosecution can later narrow the scope of the granted claims.

def: The person or entity in whom a granted patent is vested as proprietor.
ex: The patentee sought an injunction restraining the rival's sales.

def: The registered owner of an intellectual property right, entitled to exploit and enforce it.
ex: As registered proprietor of the mark, she could license its use to third parties.

def: A licence granted by a licensee to a further party, deriving from the head licence.
ex: The agreement forbade any sublicence without the licensor's prior written consent.

def: The state of a registered right failing to meet the legal conditions for its subsistence.
ex: The accused infringer pleaded invalidity, contending the mark was purely descriptive.

def: The condition of a right being void from the outset as if it had never validly existed.
ex: A finding of nullity means the registration is treated as never having conferred protection.

def: To cease to have effect, especially where renewal fees for a right are not paid.
ex: The patent lapsed when the proprietor failed to pay the fifth-year renewal fee.

def: The reinstatement of a lapsed right where the failure to renew is shown to be unintentional.
ex: The office allowed restoration of the patent on proof that the missed payment was inadvertent.

def: A formal challenge lodged with a registry to prevent or annul the grant of a right.
ex: The proprietor of the earlier mark filed an opposition against the confusingly similar application.

def: The right to rely on the filing date of an earlier application when assessing novelty of a later one.
ex: By claiming priority from the German filing, they pre-dated the intervening disclosure.

def: The capacity of a sign to distinguish the goods or services of one undertaking from those of others.
ex: The applicant showed acquired distinctiveness through decades of extensive advertising.

def: The quality of a sign that merely describes a characteristic of goods, rendering it prima facie unregistrable.
ex: The refusal rested on the descriptiveness of the word for the software's function.

def: The distinctive overall appearance or packaging of goods, capable of protection in passing-off.
ex: The rival's imitation of the distinctive get-up misled consumers about the product's origin.

def: The manufacture or sale of imitation goods bearing a mark identical to a registered one, to deceive buyers.
ex: Customs seized the container after detecting large-scale counterfeiting of the branded trainers.

def: The unauthorised copying and distribution of copyright-protected works, typically on a commercial scale.
ex: Online piracy of the film cost the studio millions in lost revenue.

def: The passing off of another's work or ideas as one's own, which may also infringe copyright.
ex: The publisher withdrew the book once the plagiarism of earlier scholarship came to light.

def: The wrongful taking or use of another's intangible property, notably trade secrets or goodwill.
ex: The former employee was sued for misappropriation of confidential manufacturing know-how.

def: The author's moral right to be identified as the creator of a work.
ex: The contract waived the illustrator's right of attribution on the commissioned artwork.

def: The requirement that a work originate from its author and reflect a degree of intellectual creation.
ex: Copyright subsisted because the compilation showed sufficient originality in its selection.

def: The recording of a work in a tangible or permanent form, often a precondition of copyright.
ex: An improvised speech attracts protection only upon fixation, such as a recording.

def: The existence of a copyright in a work as a matter of law, given that the qualifying conditions are met.
ex: The first issue was the subsistence of copyright in the database.

def: The status of being the creator of a work, from which first ownership of copyright typically flows.
ex: Joint authorship arose because both contributors shaped the final composition.

def: The determination of who actually devised the inventive concept claimed in a patent.
ex: A dispute over inventorship arose because a colleague claimed to have conceived the key step.

def: The conversion of object code back into readable form, permitted in limited cases to achieve interoperability.
ex: The directive allows decompilation only so far as necessary to make programs interoperable.

def: The ability of software or systems to work together, an aim that may justify limited copying.
ex: The lawful copying was confined to information needed to achieve interoperability with the platform.

def: A rights holder's tacit tolerance of another's use, which may bar later objection to it.
ex: Five years of acquiescence in the later mark's use extinguished the right to seek its cancellation.

def: The quality of a patent being unavoidably infringed by implementing a technical standard.
ex: The parties disputed the essentiality of several patents declared standard-essential.

def: Actively encouraging another to infringe, a basis for secondary liability in patent and copyright law.
ex: Advertising the product for the infringing use amounted to inducement of infringement.

def: A distinguishing sign or mark serving to indicate the commercial origin of goods or services.
ex: The stylised logo functioned as an indicium of origin recognised throughout the market.

def: An arrangement by which similar marks are used in parallel under agreed conditions to avoid conflict.
ex: The parties signed a coexistence agreement delimiting the territories in which each mark would be used.

def: From the very beginning, used to describe something treated as invalid or valid from its inception.
ex: Because the parties never had capacity to contract, the agreement was void ab initio.

def: Made or done in good faith, without fraud or deception.
ex: He was a bona fide purchaser for value and took the property free of the earlier charge.

def: Done in bad faith, with dishonest intent or knowledge of wrongdoing.
ex: The court found that the transfer was made mala fide to defeat the claims of creditors.

def: Denoting legal work undertaken without charge for the public good.
ex: The firm requires each associate to complete fifty hours of pro bono work every year.

def: Existing in fact, whether or not by legal right.
ex: Although never formally appointed, he acted as the de facto director of the company.

def: Existing by right or according to law, whether or not that is the position in fact.
ex: She remained the de jure owner even after losing physical possession of the land.

def: Calculated in proportion to a relevant total, such as a share or a period of time.
ex: Dividends are payable pro rata according to each shareholder's holding.

def: Let the buyer beware, the principle that a purchaser buys at their own risk absent a warranty.
ex: The doctrine of caveat emptor placed the onus on the buyer to inspect the property before completion.

def: Of its own unique kind and not fitting into any existing category.
ex: The database right is a sui generis form of protection distinct from copyright.

def: Between the parties, denoting a hearing at which both sides are present and heard.
ex: The interim order was later reconsidered at an inter partes hearing.

def: Given as a favour or gesture of goodwill rather than out of any legal obligation.
ex: The company made an ex gratia payment to the injured worker without admitting liability.

def: In the place of a parent, describing a person who assumes parental responsibility for a child.
ex: During the school trip the teachers stood in loco parentis to the pupils.

def: The principle that a person who willingly consents to a risk cannot later sue for resulting harm.
ex: The defence of volenti non fit injuria failed because the claimant had not truly consented to the danger.

def: The principle that negligence may be inferred where the accident speaks for itself.
ex: Since a swab was left inside the patient, the claimant relied on res ipsa loquitur.

def: The rule that no one may be a judge in their own cause, requiring an impartial decision-maker.
ex: Because the chairman had a financial interest, the decision offended nemo judex in causa sua.

def: The principle that agreements must be kept and are binding on the parties who make them.
ex: Under the maxim pacta sunt servanda, the state was obliged to honour the treaty.

def: The principle that there can be no punishment without a pre-existing law creating the offence.
ex: Retrospective criminal liability would violate nulla poena sine lege.

def: The burden of proof, namely the duty to establish the facts alleged.
ex: In criminal cases the onus probandi rests firmly on the prosecution.

def: The maxim that the burden of proof lies on the party who asserts, not on the one who denies.
ex: The tribunal reminded the applicant that ei incumbit probatio qui dicit governs who must prove the claim.

def: At the outset or threshold of proceedings, typically of a preliminary objection or motion.
ex: Counsel raised a motion in limine to exclude the disputed evidence before trial.

def: So trivial or minor that the law will not take account of it.
ex: The court dismissed the encroachment as de minimis and refused any remedy.

def: In agreement on the same thing, denoting the meeting of minds needed to form a contract.
ex: Because the parties were never ad idem on price, no binding contract arose.

def: The maxim that ignorance of the law is no excuse for breaking it.
ex: The defendant's plea that he did not know the regulation failed, since ignorantia juris non excusat.

def: A judge's incidental remark that is not essential to the decision and carries no binding authority.
ex: The observation was mere dictum and did not bind the courts that followed.

def: An authoritative decree or order issued by a person having the power to enforce it.
ex: The regulator cannot rewrite the parties' bargain by fiat.

def: Of an order, taking effect only after a specified period unless cause is shown to the contrary.
ex: The decree nisi would be made absolute after six weeks.

def: Simply and unconditionally; without qualification or added condition.
ex: The obligation was to deliver the goods simpliciter, not upon any precondition.

def: Used to introduce a doubtful point or an open question of law for consideration.
ex: Quaere whether the same principle applies to a gratuitous bailee.

def: Official approval or sanction giving something the authority to proceed.
ex: The scheme could not go ahead without the minister's imprimatur.

def: Signs, marks or indications from which the existence of a fact may be inferred.
ex: The document bore all the indicia of a validly executed deed.

def: A person who has made and left a valid will.
ex: The testator revoked all previous wills in the opening clause.

def: A woman who has made and left a valid will.
ex: The testatrix appointed her two daughters as her executrices.

def: Having died without leaving a valid will.
ex: Because he died intestate, his estate passed under the statutory rules.

def: A document executed to add to, vary or partly revoke an existing will.
ex: She added a codicil leaving a modest legacy to her carer.

def: A person who holds property under a usufruct.
ex: As usufructuary she was entitled to the harvest but not to fell the timber.

def: A charge or security over property that remains in the debtor's possession.
ex: The landlord's hypothec secured the arrears of rent over the tenant's goods.

def: A civil wrong giving rise to an obligation to make reparation, especially in civil-law systems.
ex: Under Scots law the claim sounded in delict rather than in contract.

def: The formal act of freeing a person from slavery or bondage.
ex: The deed of manumission granted the bondsman his liberty.

def: A person appointed to manage the affairs or property of one unable to do so.
ex: A curator was appointed to administer the estate of the incapacitated heir.

def: The right of the firstborn, especially the eldest son, to inherit the whole estate.
ex: Under the old rule of primogeniture the younger sons took nothing.

def: In accordance with or under the authority of a specified statute, contract, or provision.
ex: Pursuant to clause 12.3, the tenant shall give three months' written notice of any assignment.

word: without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing
def: Introducing specific examples that do not limit the broad scope of a general provision just stated.
ex: The Company shall keep proper records and, without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing, shall retain all invoices for six years.

def: Introducing a clarification that makes explicit something intended to be implied, removing any possible ambiguity.
ex: For the avoidance of doubt, nothing in this clause obliges the Buyer to purchase further stock.

def: Conditional upon or qualified by another provision, which takes priority in the event of conflict.
ex: Subject to clause 5, the Licensee may sub-license the software to its affiliates.

def: Except as otherwise provided in a specified place, used to carve out an exception to a general rule.
ex: Save as expressly set out in Schedule 2, all warranties are excluded to the fullest extent permitted by law.

def: Except that, introducing a single qualification to an otherwise general statement.
ex: The terms of the previous lease shall continue to apply, save that the annual rent is increased to £45,000.

def: Introducing a proviso that imposes a condition or qualification on the preceding words.
