def: Looseness or excessive slackness in a ligament or joint.
ex: Testing revealed increased laxity of the knee ligament compared with the uninjured side.

def: An abnormally large range of movement at a joint beyond the usual limits.
ex: Her generalised hypermobility meant we focused on stability and control rather than stretching.

def: Describing an angulation in which the distal part of a limb turns outward, away from the midline.
ex: On squatting, her knee collapsed into a valgus position, placing strain on the inner structures.

def: Describing an angulation in which the distal part of a limb turns inward, toward the midline.
ex: A varus alignment of the knee concentrated load on the inner compartment of the joint.

def: An inward curvature of the spine, most commonly in the lower back.
ex: An increased lumbar lordosis was noted, and we worked on core control and posture.

def: A sideways curvature of the spine.
ex: The scoliosis produced a visible asymmetry of the shoulders and waist on standing.

def: The number of steps taken per minute during walking or running.
ex: Increasing her cadence slightly reduced the load on the knee during each running stride.

def: The driving force that moves the body forward, generated as the foot pushes off.
ex: Weak calf muscles reduced propulsion, giving him a short, laboured step on that side.

def: Exercise and preparation undertaken before surgery to improve fitness and outcomes.
ex: A short prehabilitation programme before the knee replacement helped her recover more quickly afterwards.

def: The measurement of muscle strength or grip using a calibrated instrument.
ex: Hand-grip dynamometry provided a reliable baseline against which to track her recovery.

def: A wheeled walking frame, usually with brakes and a seat, used to aid mobility.
ex: With a rollator she could walk further and rest on the seat whenever she felt tired.

def: The process of restoring physical fitness and function after a period of illness or inactivity.
ex: A structured reconditioning programme gradually rebuilt his stamina after the long hospital stay.

def: A limping walking pattern adopted to avoid pain, in which less time is spent bearing weight on the affected leg.
ex: He presented with an antalgic gait, shortening the stance phase on the painful right hip.

def: A restriction allowing only a limited portion of body weight to be placed through an affected limb, usually with a walking aid.
ex: You are partial weight-bearing for six weeks, so put no more than half your weight through that foot when you use the crutches.

def: Joint movement performed by the patient with additional help from the therapist or the other limb when the muscles are too weak to complete it alone.
ex: In the early post-operative phase we used active-assisted range of motion, guiding the arm through elevation with a pulley.

def: The quality of resistance a clinician perceives at the limit of a joint's passive movement, which helps identify the structure restricting it.
ex: The knee had a hard, bony end-feel, suggesting an osteophyte rather than muscle tightness.

def: Wasting or loss of muscle bulk resulting from disuse, immobilisation, or nerve damage.
ex: Weeks in a cast had caused visible atrophy of the quadriceps, so early strengthening was a priority.

def: The therapeutic process of retraining a safe and efficient walking pattern, often after injury, surgery, or neurological insult.
ex: Gait re-education focused on achieving heel strike and even step length rather than dragging the affected foot.

def: The sequence of events from one heel strike to the next heel strike of the same foot during walking.
ex: We analysed each phase of the gait cycle to pinpoint where his knee gave way.

def: The part of the gait cycle in which the foot is in contact with the ground and bearing weight.
ex: He spent too little time in stance phase on the left because loading that hip was painful.

def: The part of the gait cycle in which the foot is off the ground and advancing forward.
ex: The foot drop meant his toes caught the floor during swing phase, so we trialled an ankle-foot orthosis.

def: A walking pattern in which the pelvis drops on the unsupported side because of weakness of the hip abductors on the stance leg.
ex: Her Trendelenburg gait pointed to weak gluteus medius, so we targeted hip abductor strengthening.

def: An inability to lift the front of the foot due to weakness or paralysis of the dorsiflexor muscles.
ex: The common peroneal nerve palsy left him with a foot drop, so he compensated by lifting the knee higher.

def: The movement of turning the sole of the foot outwards, away from the midline.
ex: Weak eversion after the sprain predisposed the ankle to rolling inwards again.

def: A stretching and strengthening technique using patterns of resisted movement and alternating contraction and relaxation to improve range and control.
ex: We used proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation to lengthen the hamstrings, contracting against resistance before easing further into the stretch.

def: A clinical assessment in which the strength of a muscle is graded by the resistance it can hold against the examiner's hand.
ex: Manual muscle testing graded his ankle dorsiflexors at three out of five, meaning movement against gravity but not resistance.

def: A zero-to-five grading system used to rate muscle strength, from no contraction to full power against resistance.
ex: On the Oxford scale the quadriceps scored four, so it could resist moderate but not full pressure.

def: A muscle-strengthening exercise in which tension is generated without any change in muscle length or visible joint movement.
ex: While the knee was too painful to bend, we began with isometric quad sets to maintain muscle activation.

def: Strengthening in which the muscle lengthens under tension, often used to rehabilitate tendon injuries.
ex: For his Achilles tendinopathy we prescribed eccentric loading, lowering the heel slowly off the edge of a step.

def: The principle of gradually increasing the demands placed on the body so that strength or endurance continues to improve.
ex: We applied progressive overload by adding a kilogram to the ankle weight each fortnight as she tolerated it.

def: A treatment technique that gently glides and tensions a nerve to restore its normal movement and reduce sensitivity.
ex: For the sciatic symptoms we introduced neural mobilisation, sliding the nerve without provoking sharp pain.

def: The manual manipulation of muscle, fascia, and other soft structures to relieve tension and improve mobility.
ex: Soft tissue mobilisation of the upper trapezius eased the tightness before we started postural retraining.

def: A manual technique using graded oscillatory or sustained movements to restore range and reduce pain at a stiff joint.
ex: Grade three joint mobilisation of the shoulder gradually improved her reach into the painful arc.

def: The application of stretchy adhesive tape to the skin to support muscles and joints or influence pain and swelling.
ex: We trialled kinesiology taping around the kneecap to give her more confidence during her return to running.

def: A programme of exercises designed to improve stability and reduce the risk of falls.
ex: Following her fall we began balance retraining, progressing from standing with support to standing on one leg.

def: An alternative way of performing a task that a patient adopts to work around a physical impairment.
ex: Until his shoulder recovered we taught a compensatory strategy for dressing, starting with the affected arm first.

def: A protective involuntary tightening of muscles around a painful or injured area.
ex: There was considerable muscle guarding of the lumbar spine, so we prioritised pain relief before hands-on treatment.

def: Abnormally increased muscle tone that makes a muscle feel tight and resistant to passive stretch.
ex: Hypertonicity of the affected arm made it difficult to position the hand for functional tasks.

def: A sturdy belt fastened around a patient's waist that a clinician holds to steady and support them during walking or transfers.
ex: I'll pop this gait belt around your waist so I can support you safely as you stand.

def: A patient's ability to move about in bed, including rolling, bridging, and moving from lying to sitting.
ex: We worked on bed mobility first, teaching him to roll onto his side before pushing up to sit.

def: A set of exercises a patient is instructed to carry out independently between clinic sessions.
ex: Your home exercise programme has three stretches to do twice a day, and I'll write them down with pictures.

def: The routine self-care tasks a person performs each day, such as washing, dressing, and feeding themselves.
ex: Our goal is for you to manage your activities of daily living, especially getting yourself dressed, without help.

def: A patient's ability to carry out everyday activities safely without assistance from another person.
ex: Rehabilitation aimed to restore enough functional independence for him to return home and live alone.

def: A temporary worsening of symptoms, particularly pain, after a period of relative stability.
ex: A flare-up after gardening is normal and doesn't mean you've caused any damage, so we'll just ease back the exercises for a few days.

def: A standardised tool or test used to quantify a patient's status and track change over the course of treatment.
ex: We repeated the Timed Up and Go as an outcome measure and it showed a clear improvement in her mobility.

def: The ability of the trunk muscles to support and control the spine and pelvis during movement.
ex: Improving core stability helped take the strain off her lower back when lifting the children.

def: The medical term for the big toe.
ex: The patient presented with pain and swelling over the hallux, consistent with a longstanding bunion.

def: Relating to the sole of the foot.
ex: I could see thickened skin across the plantar surface of the forefoot where the pressure was highest.

def: The turning of the sole of the foot inwards, towards the midline of the body.
ex: The injury happened when the ankle rolled into sudden inversion on uneven ground.

def: A bony prominence at the base of the big toe caused by the toe deviating outwards.
ex: Wider footwear may ease the pressure on the bunion, though it will not correct the deformity.

def: A fungal infection of the nail that causes thickening, discolouration and crumbling.
ex: The discoloured, brittle toenails were consistent with onychomycosis affecting several digits.

def: The condition in which a nail edge grows into the surrounding skin, commonly called an ingrown toenail.
ex: The inflamed nail sulcus and offensive discharge pointed to an infected onychocryptosis.

def: The death of body tissue due to loss of blood supply or serious infection.
ex: The blackened, mummified toe was an unmistakable sign of dry gangrene.

def: The formation of an open sore where skin or tissue has broken down.
ex: Repeated pressure over the deformed joint eventually led to ulceration of the overlying skin.

def: A spreading bacterial infection of the skin and the tissue just beneath it.
ex: The hot, red, swollen lower leg with a raised temperature suggested cellulitis.

def: Pain and tenderness in the ball of the foot beneath the long bones of the toes.
ex: She complained of metatarsalgia, a burning ache under the ball of the foot when standing.

def: Inflammation of the small bones embedded in the tendon beneath the big toe joint.
ex: Pain directly under the big toe joint on push-off pointed towards sesamoiditis.

def: A limitation of upward foot movement in which the ankle cannot bend past a right angle.
ex: A tight calf produced an ankle equinus that shifted extra load onto the forefoot.

def: Describing a foot with an abnormally high arch.
ex: In a cavus foot the raised arch concentrates pressure on the heel and the ball.

def: A congenital deformity in which the foot is twisted out of its normal position, commonly called club foot.
ex: The child was born with talipes and had worn corrective casts as an infant.

def: Relating to the joint beneath the ankle bone that allows the foot to tilt inwards and outwards.
ex: Restricted subtalar movement limits how well the foot can adapt to uneven ground.

def: The heel bone, the largest bone of the foot.
ex: The fall from height had fractured the calcaneus, making weight-bearing impossible.

def: Relating to the heel bone.
ex: A calcaneal spur is a small bony outgrowth on the underside of the heel bone.

def: Any of the five long bones connecting the ankle to the toes.
ex: A stress fracture of the second metatarsal is common after a sudden increase in walking.

def: Any of the small bones that make up the toes.
ex: The joint between the two bones of the phalanx had become stiff and swollen.

def: Situated or occurring between the toes or fingers.
ex: The interdigital skin was soft and white, a sign of moisture trapped between the toes.

def: A fungal infection of the skin, such as the type affecting the feet known as athlete's foot.
ex: The itchy, peeling skin between the toes was typical of tinea.

def: A thin, flexible fibre pressed against the skin to test whether protective sensation is present.
ex: When the patient could not feel the monofilament on several sites, we recorded a loss of protective sensation.

def: Describing a foot affected by both nerve damage and a poor blood supply.
ex: A neuroischaemic foot combines numbness with poor circulation, so wounds are both painless and slow to heal.

def: A marked reduction in the motivation to initiate and sustain purposeful, goal-directed activity, recognised as a negative symptom of schizophrenia.
ex: His avolition was so profound that he would sit unwashed for days, unable to muster the drive to attend even to basic self-care.

def: A poverty of speech, with a reduction in the amount or informational content of what is said, occurring as a negative symptom of psychosis.
ex: Her alogia rendered the interview laborious, as each open question elicited only a monosyllabic, impoverished reply.

def: A pathological loss of will, drive or initiative in which a person is unable to make decisions or act spontaneously.
ex: Following the frontal infarct he sank into an abulia so complete that he would leave a ringing phone unanswered beside him.

def: A psychomotor syndrome characterised by features such as stupor, mutism, posturing, negativism and waxy flexibility.
ex: The patient's catatonia responded dramatically to a lorazepam challenge, and within an hour she was speaking and moving freely again.

def: A chronic, low-grade depressive disorder in which depressed mood persists for most of the day for at least two years.
ex: Her dysthymia had smouldered for a decade, never disabling but leaving her joyless and perpetually flat.

def: A chronic mood disturbance marked by fluctuating subsyndromal hypomanic and depressive symptoms that never meet the full threshold for either pole.
ex: His cyclothymia produced weeks of buoyant productivity followed by shallow troughs, none severe enough to warrant hospitalisation.

def: A stable, normal mood state that is neither depressed nor elevated.
ex: After six months on the mood stabiliser she had maintained euthymia, with no relapse into either mania or depression.

def: An antipsychotic drug used to treat psychosis, so named for its dampening effect on psychomotor activity.
ex: The older neuroleptic controlled his hallucinations but left him with a disabling tremor and stiffness.

def: Describing a substance that acts on the mind to alter mood, perception or behaviour.
ex: A careful review of his psychotropic medication revealed three agents with overlapping sedative effects.

def: A sense that one's surroundings are unreal, distant or dreamlike.
ex: During the panic attack she was gripped by derealisation, as though the room and everyone in it were behind glass.

def: A pattern of speech that is over-inclusive and laden with irrelevant detail but eventually returns to the point.
ex: The interview was protracted by his circumstantiality, each answer meandering through tangents before finally addressing the question.

def: The automatic, meaningless repetition of words or phrases spoken by another person.
ex: The child's echolalia meant that questions were parroted back verbatim rather than answered.

def: A newly coined word or expression whose meaning is idiosyncratic to the speaker and unintelligible to others, seen in psychosis.
ex: Scattered through his account were neologisms such as 'trancifying', words that carried private significance but no shared meaning.

def: An excessive, often incoherent flow of speech that is difficult to interrupt.
ex: In his manic state his logorrhoea was relentless, the words tumbling out faster than any listener could follow.

def: The therapeutic release of repressed emotion achieved by reliving the experience that produced it.
ex: The guided abreaction allowed her to discharge the terror she had walled off since the assault.

def: The therapist's redirection of their own feelings and unconscious reactions onto the patient.
ex: In supervision she recognised that her irritation with the patient was countertransference echoing her own family dynamics.

def: The unconscious redirection of feelings about a significant figure from one's past onto the therapist.
ex: The intense transference became a central tool of the therapy, as she began to treat the analyst like her withholding father.

def: The expression of psychological distress through physical symptoms for which no adequate organic cause is found.
ex: Years of somatisation had brought her to countless specialists, each investigation for her abdominal pain returning normal.

def: A persistent, excessive preoccupation with the fear of having a serious illness, despite reassurance.
ex: His hypochondriasis transformed every benign palpitation into conviction of imminent cardiac death.

def: The deliberate fabrication or gross exaggeration of symptoms motivated by an external incentive such as compensation or avoiding duty.
ex: The inconsistencies between his reported disability and his observed behaviour raised the question of malingering.

def: A non-fatal act of self-injury or self-poisoning that resembles suicide but is carried out without a definite fatal intent.
ex: Repeated episodes of parasuicide by superficial cutting reflected her distress rather than a settled wish to die.

def: A profound lack of energy and physical or mental drive, characteristic of depression.
ex: The anergia of her depression was crushing, so that even lifting a cup felt like an insurmountable effort.

def: Excessive daytime sleepiness or prolonged night-time sleep that is not relieved by rest.
ex: His atypical depression presented with hypersomnia, and he was sleeping upwards of twelve hours yet waking unrefreshed.

def: Any of a group of abnormal behaviours or experiences that occur during sleep or the transitions into and out of it.
ex: His night terrors and sleepwalking were classified as a parasomnia arising from slow-wave sleep.

def: A disorder characterised by the recurrent, irresistible urge to pull out one's own hair, resulting in noticeable hair loss.
ex: Her trichotillomania had left a patch of alopecia at the crown, which she concealed carefully with a scarf.

def: A preoccupying and distressing belief that some aspect of one's appearance is grossly defective, though it appears normal to others.
ex: His body dysmorphia fixated on an imagined asymmetry of his nose, driving repeated requests for surgery.

def: A recurrent failure to resist impulses to steal objects that are not needed for personal use or monetary value.
ex: Her kleptomania compelled her to pocket trinkets she neither wanted nor could explain, followed by intense shame.

def: An uncontrollable, often episodic craving for alcohol.
ex: His dipsomania took the form of periodic binges separated by weeks of complete abstinence.

def: A reversible impairment of cognition that mimics dementia but is caused by a psychiatric disorder, most often depression.
ex: Her apparent memory loss proved to be a depressive pseudodementia that resolved once her mood was treated.

def: A worsening of confusion, agitation and restlessness that occurs in the late afternoon and evening in people with dementia.
ex: Staff learned to anticipate her sundowning, dimming the ward lights and reducing stimulation as dusk approached.

def: An impaired ability to recognise familiar faces despite intact vision and general intellect.
ex: His prosopagnosia meant he identified his own wife only by her voice and the coat she habitually wore.

def: A difficulty in retrieving words, particularly the names of objects, despite otherwise fluent speech.
ex: The anomia surfaced during naming tests, when he could describe a watch's function yet not summon the word.

def: Relating to or acting upon neurotransmission mediated by serotonin.
ex: Combining two serotonergic agents raised the spectre of serotonin syndrome, so the doses were staggered carefully.

def: The reabsorption of a released neurotransmitter by the presynaptic neuron that secreted it.
ex: The antidepressant works by blocking the reuptake of serotonin, prolonging its action in the synaptic cleft.

def: A process whereby repeated subthreshold stimulation progressively lowers the threshold for a response, invoked to explain worsening withdrawal and recurrent mood episodes.
ex: The kindling hypothesis suggests each successive episode of depression becomes easier to trigger and harder to arrest.

def: A loss or marked poverty of voluntary movement.
ex: The akinesia induced by the antipsychotic left him masklike and immobile, initially mistaken for depressive withdrawal.

def: A syndrome of tremor, rigidity and slowness of movement that may be caused by disease or, commonly, by antipsychotic drugs.
ex: The cogwheel rigidity and shuffling gait were recognised as drug-induced parkinsonism and prompted a dose reduction.

def: A mature defence mechanism by which unacceptable impulses are unconsciously channelled into socially valued activity.
ex: Through sublimation he redirected his aggression into competitive boxing rather than into open conflict.

def: An excessive instability of emotion, with rapid and disproportionate shifts of mood.
ex: The emotional lability that followed his stroke had him weeping and laughing within the space of a single conversation.

def: A repetitive, purposeless movement or utterance that is carried out in a uniform, mechanical way.
ex: The rhythmic rocking was a stereotypy that appeared to soothe him during periods of overstimulation.

def: The simultaneous existence of contradictory feelings or attitudes towards the same object or situation.
ex: Her deep ambivalence about recovery surfaced whenever discharge was raised, as she both craved and dreaded independence.

def: A purging release of pent-up emotion that brings a sense of relief.
ex: Recounting the trauma in a safe setting brought a catharsis that visibly lightened her demeanour.

def: The capacity to understand behaviour in terms of underlying mental states in oneself and others.
ex: The therapy sought to strengthen her mentalisation, helping her read her partner's intentions rather than assuming rejection.

def: The provision of structured information to patients and families about a mental disorder and its management.
ex: Simple psychoeducation about the warning signs of relapse enabled the family to seek help far earlier.

def: An inability or refusal to speak in the absence of a structural cause for the loss of speech.
ex: Her selective mutism meant she conversed freely at home yet uttered not a word in the classroom.

def: A trance-like state of rigid immobility in which the body maintains whatever posture it is placed in.
ex: In his catalepsy the arm remained aloft for minutes after the examiner had raised it, held as if by an unseen splint.

def: A state of heightened physiological and psychological alertness, comprising a cluster of symptoms central to post-traumatic stress disorder.
ex: His hyperarousal manifested as an exaggerated startle response and a constant scanning of the room for threats.

def: The production of still images of internal structures by passing X-rays through the body onto a detector.
ex: Plain radiography of the chest was requested before the patient was referred for further imaging.

def: A technique that uses a continuous X-ray beam to display moving internal structures in real time on a screen.
ex: During fluoroscopy the radiologist watched the contrast pass through the bowel in real time.

def: An imaging method that produces cross-sectional slices of the body from many angled projections.
ex: Computed tomography gave a series of thin axial slices through the abdomen.

def: The use of high-frequency sound waves to generate images of soft tissues and organs.
ex: Abdominal sonography was chosen first because it avoids ionising radiation.

def: A nuclear-medicine technique that maps the distribution of an injected radioactive tracer using a gamma camera.
ex: Bone scintigraphy highlighted areas of increased tracer uptake in the spine.

def: Low-dose X-ray imaging of the breast used chiefly for screening and assessment.
ex: She was recalled from the screening programme for further mammography of the left breast.

def: The measurement of tissue density, most often bone mineral density, from an imaging examination.
ex: Bone densitometry was arranged to assess the patient's fracture risk.

def: An imaging technique that measures the stiffness or elasticity of tissue.
ex: Liver elastography estimated the degree of tissue stiffness without a biopsy.

def: A particular method or type of medical imaging, such as ultrasound, CT or MRI.
ex: The team discussed which imaging modality would answer the clinical question with the least radiation.

def: The specific direction in which the X-ray beam passes through the body to form a view.
ex: An additional lateral projection was taken to confirm the position of the device.

def: Positioned or projected at a slanting angle rather than straight on.
ex: An oblique view separated the overlapping structures that obscured the straight projection.

def: A position in which the patient lies on one side, often used to detect free fluid or air.
ex: A left lateral decubitus film was taken to demonstrate a small pleural effusion.

def: In an upright, standing or sitting position during imaging.
ex: An erect chest film is preferred for showing free gas beneath the diaphragm.

def: Directed towards the head end of the body.
ex: The beam was angled cephalad to project the clavicles above the lung apices.

def: Directed towards the feet or tail end of the body.
ex: Angling the tube caudad opened up the disc spaces on the lumbar film.

def: Movement of a limb away from the midline of the body.
ex: Shoulder abduction was needed to bring the joint clear of the ribs.

def: The bending of a joint that decreases the angle between two bones.
ex: Lateral views in flexion and extension assessed movement between the vertebrae.

def: Appearing white on an X-ray because the structure absorbs, rather than transmits, radiation.
ex: The swallowed coin was clearly radiopaque against the softer surrounding tissue.

def: Appearing dark on an X-ray because the structure allows radiation to pass through easily.
ex: Gas in the bowel is radiolucent and shows as dark areas on the film.

def: An area on an image that appears whiter than expected because it blocks more radiation.
ex: A rounded opacity was noted in the right lower zone and warranted comparison with old films.

def: The process by which a region becomes denser and whiter on an image, often after contrast.
ex: Opacification of the collecting system confirmed that the contrast had reached the kidney.

def: A darker area on an image where less radiation has been absorbed than in the surrounding tissue.
ex: A thin lucency around the implant raised the question of loosening.

def: The reduction in intensity of a beam as it passes through and is absorbed by tissue.
ex: Dense bone causes greater attenuation of the X-ray beam than soft tissue does.

def: The increase in image brightness of a structure after a contrast agent has been given.
ex: The lesion showed avid enhancement after intravenous contrast was administered.

def: Appearing brighter or whiter than the surrounding tissue on a cross-sectional scan.
ex: A hyperdense area on the unenhanced scan suggested fresh bleeding.

def: Appearing darker than the surrounding tissue on a cross-sectional scan.
ex: A hypodense region within the organ was reported and correlated with the ultrasound.

def: Producing strong reflections and therefore appearing bright on an ultrasound image.
ex: The echogenic focus cast an acoustic shadow typical of a small stone.

def: Appearing brighter than the surrounding tissue on ultrasound because it reflects more sound.
ex: The mass was hyperechoic relative to the adjacent liver.

def: Appearing black on ultrasound because it reflects no sound, as with clear fluid.
ex: The cyst was anechoic with well-defined walls and posterior brightening.

def: Describing bone that appears abnormally dense and white on imaging.
ex: A sclerotic focus in the vertebra was noted and compared with previous studies.

def: Describing an area where bone has been destroyed and appears darker than normal.
ex: A lytic area in the pelvis prompted correlation with the clinical history.

def: The deposition of calcium in tissue, which appears dense and white on imaging.
ex: Fine calcification within the vessel wall was visible on the plain film.

def: A region of lung in which the air spaces have filled, producing an area of opacity.
ex: Consolidation in the right lower lobe was consistent with the clinical picture.

def: Enlargement of the heart, assessed on imaging by its size relative to the chest.
ex: The film showed cardiomegaly, with the heart occupying more than half the chest width.

def: Dilatation of the kidney's collecting system, usually from obstructed urine flow.
ex: Ultrasound revealed mild hydronephrosis on the left side.

def: The restriction of the X-ray beam to the area of interest to reduce dose and scatter.
ex: Tight collimation to the wrist kept the dose to surrounding tissue as low as possible.

def: To narrow and confine the X-ray beam to the region being imaged.
ex: Always collimate closely to the joint so that unnecessary tissue is not irradiated.

def: A device worn by staff to measure their cumulative exposure to ionising radiation.
ex: Every radiographer must wear a dosimeter at collar level throughout the shift.

def: The calculation and measurement of radiation dose received by a patient or worker.
ex: Careful dosimetry ensures that the dose stays within recommended limits.

def: Protective material used to reduce radiation reaching sensitive tissues or bystanders.
ex: Lead shielding was placed over the patient before the exposure was made.

def: Radiation that is deflected back towards its source after striking tissue or a surface.
ex: Standing behind the lead screen protects staff from backscatter during the procedure.

def: A sampling artefact in which fast flow or fine detail is mismapped, distorting the image.
ex: Aliasing on the Doppler trace was corrected by adjusting the velocity scale.

def: A lesion found unexpectedly on imaging performed for an unrelated reason.
ex: The report described a small adrenal incidentaloma that required no immediate action.

def: Open and unobstructed, said of a vessel, duct or airway on imaging.
ex: The vessel remained patent, with contrast flowing freely through it.

def: Having many twists and bends, typically said of an elongated blood vessel.
ex: The aorta appeared tortuous and unfolded, a common finding with age.

def: The hand-held probe that both emits and receives sound waves during ultrasound.
ex: A little more gel was applied so the transducer made good contact with the skin.

def: The quantitative scale of radiodensity used on CT, calibrated so that water measures zero and air measures minus one thousand.
ex: A value of minus ninety Hounsfield units confirmed the adrenal nodule was a lipid-rich adenoma.

def: Appearing lower in density, and therefore darker, than the surrounding tissue on CT.
ex: A wedge-shaped hypoattenuating area in the spleen was in keeping with an infarct.

def: Of a density similar to that of the adjacent tissue, which can make a lesion difficult to distinguish on CT.
ex: The subacute subdural haematoma was nearly isodense to cortex, making it easy to overlook.

def: Producing fewer echoes and therefore appearing darker than surrounding tissue on ultrasound.
ex: A hypoechoic thyroid nodule with irregular margins warranted fine-needle aspiration.

def: The degree to which a tissue reflects ultrasound waves and thus its relative brightness on the image.
ex: Increased renal cortical echogenicity was noted, in keeping with chronic parenchymal disease.

def: The dark band seen deep to a structure that strongly reflects or absorbs ultrasound, such as a gallstone or calcification.
ex: A mobile echogenic focus casting clean acoustic shadowing confirmed a gallstone.

def: The apparent increase in echoes seen deep to a fluid-filled structure on ultrasound, owing to reduced attenuation.
ex: Posterior acoustic enhancement behind the breast lesion favoured a cyst over a solid mass.

def: Describing an MRI sequence in which fluid and many pathological tissues appear bright.
ex: On the T2-weighted images, the cord lesion returned high signal suggestive of demyelination.

def: Appearing bright, or of high signal, on a given MRI sequence.
ex: Multiple hyperintense white-matter lesions were seen on the FLAIR sequence.

def: Appearing dark, or of low signal, on a given MRI sequence.
ex: The haemosiderin rim was markedly hypointense on the gradient-echo images.

def: Reduced movement of water molecules on diffusion-weighted imaging, a hallmark of acute infarction and abscess.
ex: The lesion showed restricted diffusion with corresponding low ADC values, confirming an acute infarct.

def: A hazy increase in lung attenuation on CT that does not obscure the underlying vessels or bronchial walls.
ex: Bilateral peripheral ground-glass opacities were consistent with atypical pneumonia.

def: The appearance of air-filled bronchi made visible against surrounding opacified lung.
ex: The presence of air bronchograms within the opacity favoured consolidation over a pleural effusion.

def: Clustered cystic airspaces with thick walls on CT, indicating end-stage pulmonary fibrosis.
ex: Basal, subpleural honeycombing supported a diagnosis of usual interstitial pneumonia.

def: A branching, nodular pattern of small-airway disease on CT, resembling a budding tree.
ex: A tree-in-bud pattern in the right upper lobe raised the possibility of endobronchial spread of tuberculosis.

def: An abnormal accumulation of fluid within the pleural space.
ex: A moderate right pleural effusion blunted the costophrenic angle on the erect chest film.

def: An area within a contrast-filled lumen or structure that fails to opacify, often representing thrombus or tumour.
ex: A filling defect in the right pulmonary artery on CTPA confirmed a pulmonary embolus.

def: The adjustment of the greyscale display range, by setting window width and level, to optimise contrast for a given tissue.
ex: On bone windowing, a subtle undisplaced fracture of the transverse process became apparent.

def: Falling within the expected normal range for the appearance or measurement being assessed.
ex: Cardiac size and mediastinal contours are within normal limits.

def: The displacement or distortion of adjacent structures caused by a space-occupying lesion.
ex: The tumour exerted mass effect on the lateral ventricle with effacement of the adjacent sulci.

def: Displacement of the normally central brain structures across the midline, usually by a mass or haemorrhage.
ex: There was five millimetres of midline shift to the left secondary to the acute haematoma.

def: A lesion with a peripheral rim of contrast enhancement surrounding a non-enhancing centre.
ex: A solitary ring-enhancing lesion in the frontal lobe prompted a differential of abscess versus metastasis.

def: An area of bone destruction that appears lucent, or darker, on a radiograph.
ex: Multiple punched-out lytic lesions in the skull were suspicious for myeloma.

def: An area of increased bone density appearing whiter than normal bone on a radiograph.
ex: A solitary sclerotic lesion in the pelvis was most likely a benign bone island.

def: New bone formation at the periosteum in response to injury, infection or tumour.
ex: An aggressive, sunburst periosteal reaction raised concern for osteosarcoma.

def: Having fine radiating lines projecting from a margin, a feature that is suspicious for malignancy.
ex: A spiculated mass in the upper outer quadrant was assigned a high BI-RADS category.

def: Having sharply defined, distinct margins that separate the lesion clearly from adjacent tissue.
ex: The well-circumscribed hepatic lesion with peripheral nodular enhancement was typical of a haemangioma.

def: Hazy increased attenuation within fat on CT, indicating adjacent inflammation or oedema.
ex: Pericolonic fat stranding around a thick-walled diverticulum supported acute diverticulitis.

def: The presence of free gas within the peritoneal cavity, often signifying a perforated viscus.
ex: Free air under the diaphragm indicated pneumoperitoneum from a perforated duodenal ulcer.

def: Showing increased uptake of the radiotracer fluorodeoxyglucose on PET, reflecting high metabolic activity.
ex: A markedly FDG-avid mediastinal node was highly suspicious for nodal metastasis.

def: A semiquantitative measure of radiotracer uptake on PET used to characterise and follow lesions.
ex: The maximum standardised uptake value rose on the follow-up scan, indicating disease progression.

def: A reconstruction technique that displays the highest-attenuation voxels along each viewing ray, useful for vessels.
ex: The maximum intensity projection images clearly depicted the anomalous coronary origin.

def: The loss of signal from rapidly flowing blood, appearing dark on conventional spin-echo MRI.
ex: Prominent serpiginous flow voids indicated the nidus of an arteriovenous malformation.

def: A standard reporting recommendation to interpret the imaging findings in the light of the patient's clinical picture.
ex: The nonspecific white-matter changes are of uncertain significance; please correlate clinically.

def: The virtual absence of urine production, usually defined as less than 100 millilitres per day.
ex: Sudden anuria after the vascular surgery pointed to bilateral renal artery occlusion.

def: The slow, painful passage of urine drop by drop, accompanied by a distressing spasm of the bladder.
ex: The bladder tumour eroded the trigone, producing intractable strangury and frank haematuria.

def: The presence of pus, or excess white blood cells, in the urine.
ex: Sterile pyuria with negative cultures should prompt consideration of renal tuberculosis.

def: The presence of crystals in the urine, sometimes preceding or accompanying stone formation.
ex: Marked crystalluria on microscopy supported the diagnosis of primary hyperoxaluria.

def: The presence of the muscle pigment myoglobin in the urine, typically following muscle breakdown.
ex: The tea-coloured urine of myoglobinuria after his crush injury heralded impending acute kidney injury.

def: The presence of free haemoglobin in the urine, arising from marked intravascular haemolysis.
ex: The dark morning urine of paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria reflected complement-mediated haemolysis.

def: The excretion of urine whose osmolality is fixed at that of plasma, reflecting a lost capacity to concentrate or dilute.
ex: Isosthenuria with a urine osmolality stuck near 300 confirmed advanced tubular dysfunction.

def: An excess of nitrogenous waste products such as urea in the blood, reflecting impaired renal excretion.
ex: Prerenal azotaemia from dehydration resolved promptly once intravenous fluids restored renal perfusion.

def: The clinical syndrome of advanced renal failure, caused by retention of urea and other toxins.
ex: Encephalopathy, pericarditis and pruritus signalled that his uraemia now demanded urgent dialysis.

def: The excretion of sodium in the urine, particularly when increased above normal.
ex: Loop diuretics promote a brisk natriuresis by blocking sodium reabsorption in the ascending limb.

def: An increased production and excretion of urine.
ex: A post-obstructive diuresis followed relief of the blocked ureter, mandating careful fluid replacement.

def: To pass urine; to empty the bladder.
ex: He was unable to micturate for twelve hours after the anaesthetic and required catheterisation.

def: The involuntary passage of urine, most often used of bed-wetting in children beyond the expected age of continence.
ex: Primary nocturnal enuresis in an otherwise well seven-year-old was managed initially with an alarm.

def: The functional unit of the kidney, comprising a glomerulus and its associated tubule.
ex: Each human kidney contains roughly a million nephrons, a reserve that masks early functional decline.

def: The tuft of capillaries within the nephron where blood is filtered to form the primary urine.
ex: Immune complexes deposited in the glomerulus triggered the proliferative changes seen on biopsy.

def: The formation or presence of calculi within the kidney.
ex: Recurrent calcium-oxalate nephrolithiasis prompted a full metabolic stone screen.

def: The formation of stones anywhere within the urinary tract.
ex: Chronic dehydration in hot climates markedly raises the incidence of urolithiasis.

def: The diffuse deposition of calcium salts within the substance of the kidney.
ex: The ultrasound showed medullary nephrocalcinosis consistent with distal renal tubular acidosis.

def: Abnormal distension of the ureter with urine, usually due to a distal obstruction.
ex: Both hydroureter and hydronephrosis regressed once the pelvic mass was resected.

def: Inflammation of the kidney and its pelvis, typically from ascending bacterial infection.
ex: Loin pain, rigors and a high fever pointed to acute pyelonephritis rather than simple cystitis.

def: Inflammation of the glomeruli, an important cause of both nephritic and nephrotic presentations.
ex: A crescentic glomerulonephritis on biopsy explained his rapidly deteriorating renal function.

def: Hardening of the kidney due to sclerosis of its small blood vessels, characteristically from chronic hypertension.
ex: Decades of untreated hypertension had produced a shrunken kidney with hypertensive nephrosclerosis.

def: Originating in or produced by the kidney, or arising from an intrinsic renal defect.
ex: Lithium-induced nephrogenic diabetes insipidus reflects tubular resistance to antidiuretic hormone.

def: Relating to or caused by the accumulation of urea and other toxins in renal failure.
ex: A uraemic pericardial rub is an ominous indication for urgent dialysis.

def: Situated around or surrounding the kidney.
ex: Contrast imaging revealed a perinephric abscess tracking from the infected upper pole.

def: Relating to the specialised epithelium that lines the urinary tract.
ex: Cystoscopy and biopsy confirmed a high-grade urothelial carcinoma of the bladder.

def: Relating to the renal tubules and the surrounding interstitial tissue rather than the glomeruli.
ex: An acute tubulointerstitial nephritis was attributed to the recently started proton-pump inhibitor.

def: The smooth muscle of the bladder wall whose contraction expels urine.
ex: Detrusor overactivity produced the urgency and frequency typical of an overactive bladder.

def: The smooth triangular area of the bladder base bounded by the two ureteric orifices and the urethral opening.
ex: The tumour was sited on the trigone, close to both ureteric orifices.

def: The transitional epithelium lining the renal pelvis, ureters, bladder and proximal urethra.
ex: The urothelium stretches to accommodate a full bladder without breaching its barrier function.

def: One of the cup-shaped cavities of the renal pelvis that collect urine from the papillae.
ex: A staghorn calculus had cast branching extensions into every calyx of the kidney.

def: The conical apex of a renal pyramid, through which urine drains into a minor calyx.
ex: Sloughing of a necrotic papilla in analgesic nephropathy can obstruct the ureter.

def: The muscular tube conveying urine from the kidney to the bladder.
ex: The stone lodged at the vesicoureteric junction, the narrowest point of the ureter.

def: The canal through which urine is discharged from the bladder to the exterior.
ex: The considerably longer male urethra makes ascending infection less common than in women.

def: Inflammation of the bladder, most commonly due to bacterial infection.
ex: Uncomplicated cystitis in a young woman was treated with a short course of nitrofurantoin.

def: Inflammation of the urethra, frequently of sexually transmitted origin.
ex: Non-gonococcal urethritis is most often caused by Chlamydia trachomatis.

def: Inflammation of the prostate gland, which may be acute or chronic.
ex: Acute bacterial prostatitis presented with fever, perineal pain and an exquisitely tender gland.

def: Endoscopic examination of the interior of the bladder using a cystoscope.
ex: Flexible cystoscopy under local anaesthetic is standard for investigating visible haematuria.

def: The surgical removal of a kidney, in whole or in part.
ex: A radical nephrectomy was performed for the large renal cell carcinoma.

def: A surgically created channel draining urine directly from the renal pelvis through the skin.
ex: A percutaneous nephrostomy was inserted to decompress the obstructed, infected kidney.

def: The fragmentation of urinary calculi, classically by focused shock waves applied through the body wall.
ex: Extracorporeal shock-wave lithotripsy shattered the renal stone into passable fragments.

def: A technique of blood purification in which solutes are cleared across a semipermeable membrane in an external circuit.
ex: He commenced thrice-weekly haemodialysis once his kidney function fell below ten per cent.

def: A continuous renal replacement technique that removes solutes and water by convective transport across a filter.
ex: The haemodynamically unstable patient tolerated continuous haemofiltration far better than intermittent dialysis.

def: The removal of water from the blood across a membrane under a pressure gradient, as occurs in the glomerulus or during dialysis.
ex: Aggressive ultrafiltration during dialysis relieved the fluid overload but precipitated cramps.

def: A sudden decline in kidney function over hours to days, marked by a rise in serum creatinine or a fall in urine output.
ex: His acute kidney injury was likely pre-renal, secondary to dehydration and the NSAIDs he had been taking.

def: Progressive, long-standing loss of kidney function, staged from 1 to 5 according to the estimated glomerular filtration rate.
ex: The patient has stage 4 chronic kidney disease and is being worked up for dialysis access.

def: The final stage of chronic kidney disease in which the kidneys can no longer sustain life without dialysis or transplantation.
ex: Once she reached end-stage renal disease, the team began preparing her for a living-donor transplant.

def: The volume of blood filtered by the kidneys per minute, used as the key measure of overall kidney function.
ex: We stage chronic kidney disease according to the estimated glomerular filtration rate.

def: A waste product of muscle metabolism measured in the blood as a marker of kidney function.
ex: Her serum creatinine has doubled since admission, which is concerning for worsening renal function.

def: A nitrogenous waste product excreted by the kidneys whose blood level rises when renal function declines.
ex: Both urea and creatinine were markedly raised, in keeping with significant renal impairment.

def: Blood in the urine that is visible to the naked eye and colours the urine red or pink.
ex: He was admitted with frank haematuria and clot retention after his catheter came out.

def: The need to pass urine more often than normal, whether or not the volume each time is increased.
ex: He complained of urinary frequency and nocturia, which we attributed to an enlarged prostate.

def: A sudden, compelling need to pass urine that is difficult to defer.
ex: Urgency with occasional leakage suggested an overactive bladder rather than a stress problem.

def: The inability to empty the bladder fully or at all, requiring catheterisation to relieve it.
ex: He went into acute urinary retention and we drained over a litre on catheterisation.

def: The involuntary leakage of urine, which may be stress-related, urge-related or mixed.
ex: Her stress incontinence worsened after the birth, so we referred her to the continence team.

def: An infection anywhere along the urinary tract, most commonly affecting the bladder.
ex: We sent a mid-stream urine sample before starting empirical antibiotics for the urinary tract infection.

def: Severe, spasmodic loin-to-groin pain caused by a stone obstructing the ureter.

def: To involve more senior clinicians or a higher level of monitoring when a patient's condition worsens.
ex: When the patient became increasingly hypotensive, the nurse escalated care by activating the rapid response team.

def: The structured transfer of responsibility and clinical information about a patient from one nurse or team to another.
ex: During handoff the outgoing nurse used the SBAR format to communicate the patient's deteriorating renal function.

def: To make a disease, symptom or situation more severe or worse.
ex: Excessive fluid intake may exacerbate the edema in a patient with congestive heart failure.

def: Difficult or laboured breathing that is perceived as uncomfortable or distressing by the patient.
ex: The patient reported worsening dyspnea on exertion, becoming breathless after walking only a few meters.

def: An abnormal accumulation of fluid in the tissues, causing swelling that is often first noticed in the lower limbs.
ex: The nurse noted pitting edema to mid-calf and elevated the patient's legs to promote venous return.

def: To speak or act on behalf of a patient to protect their rights, preferences and best interests.
ex: The nurse advocated for the patient by requesting an interpreter so that consent could be truly informed.

def: An abbreviation of the Latin nil per os, meaning the patient is to have nothing by mouth.
ex: The patient was kept NPO from midnight in preparation for the morning endoscopy.

def: Immediately and without delay, from the Latin statim, used for orders that must be carried out at once.
ex: The physician ordered a stat dose of epinephrine when the patient developed anaphylaxis.

def: The main symptom or concern, usually in the patient's own words, that has prompted them to seek care.
ex: The chief complaint documented on admission was crushing central chest pain radiating to the left arm.

def: An abnormality of gait or stance arising from pain or a mechanical problem in one or more limbs.
ex: The owner reported a sudden lameness in the horse's near foreleg after it had been turned out overnight.

def: The process of giving birth or expelling offspring from the uterus.
ex: We monitored the ewe closely as parturition approached in case she needed assistance.

def: The care, management and breeding of animals, including housing, feeding and general welfare.
ex: Many of the herd's problems traced back to poor husbandry rather than to any single infection.

def: The humane ending of an animal's life to relieve incurable suffering.
ex: I gently raised euthanasia as an option and gave the owner time to consider what was kindest for their dog.

def: To surgically remove an animal's reproductive organs so that it can no longer breed.
ex: I recommended that we neuter the young tom to reduce roaming and spraying behaviour.

def: To surgically remove the ovaries, and usually the uterus, of a female animal to prevent breeding.
ex: We usually spay the bitch once she has finished growing, and I talked the owner through the procedure.

def: To surgically remove the testicles of a male animal.
ex: The colt will be easier to handle once we castrate him, I told the owner.

def: A parasite, such as a flea, tick or mite, that lives on the outside of its host.
ex: The intense scratching pointed to an ectoparasite, so I examined the coat closely.

def: Partial or complete loss of hair or fur from areas where it is normally present.
ex: I noted symmetrical alopecia over both flanks and discussed possible underlying causes with the owner.

def: Abnormally thin and wasted, usually from prolonged undernutrition or chronic disease.
ex: The stray cat was emaciated, with its ribs and spine clearly visible beneath the coat.

def: The state of an animal lying down and being unable or unwilling to rise.
ex: The cow's prolonged recumbency after calving was a serious concern that needed urgent assessment.

def: An abnormal accumulation of gas in the stomach or rumen causing dangerous distension.
ex: I warned the farmer that bloat can develop rapidly and is a genuine emergency in cattle.

def: Inflammation of the mammary gland or udder, usually caused by infection.
ex: The dairy cow's swollen, painful quarter and altered milk were classic signs of mastitis.

def: The measures taken to prevent the introduction and spread of infectious disease on a farm or premises.
ex: Tightening biosecurity, such as footbaths and visitor controls, helped the farm reduce repeated outbreaks.

def: To remove or slaughter selected animals from a group, often for disease control or on welfare grounds.
ex: The vet and farmer agreed to cull the chronically infected ewes to protect the wider flock.

def: A post-mortem examination of an animal to determine the cause of death or disease.
ex: A necropsy on the fallen calf helped us identify the problem before it spread through the herd.

def: The overall shape, structure and proportions of an animal's body.
ex: Poor limb conformation predisposed the dog to joint strain as it grew.

def: The ridge between the shoulder blades of a horse or dog, used as a reference point for measuring height.
ex: We measured the pony to the withers to check it fell within the height limit.

def: A vestigial digit set higher up the leg of a dog or cat that does not normally touch the ground.
ex: The torn dewclaw was bleeding, so I explained how to keep it clean while it healed.

def: The joint on the hind leg of a quadruped corresponding to the human ankle.
ex: The swelling around the horse's hock suggested strain in that joint.

def: The single mammary organ of a cow, goat or sheep, from which milk is drawn.
ex: I examined the udder for heat, swelling or hardness before ruling out mastitis.

def: A castrated male horse.
ex: The owner preferred a gelding because it was likely to be calmer and easier to handle.

def: A young female cow that has not yet had a calf.
ex: I examined the in-calf heifer and gave the farmer advice ahead of her first calving.

def: The recurring period of sexual receptivity and fertility in a female mammal; being on heat.
ex: I explained the typical signs of oestrus so the owner would know when the bitch was fertile.

def: A serious infection of the uterus in which pus accumulates, most often in unspayed females.
ex: The older, unspayed bitch's lethargy and discharge raised my suspicion of pyometra.

def: A painful inflammatory condition of the sensitive tissues within the hoof, seen especially in horses and ponies.
ex: The pony's reluctance to move and shifting of weight made me suspect laminitis.

def: A skin disease of animals caused by parasitic mites, marked by itching and hair loss.
ex: The fox's crusted, hairless skin was a textbook picture of mange.

def: Irritable, difficult to handle or inclined to resist restraint.
ex: The cat became fractious on the table, so I asked the owner to help keep it calm.

def: Of an illness, coming on suddenly and lasting a short time.
ex: He was admitted with acute abdominal pain.

def: Of a condition, persisting for a long time or recurring.
ex: She manages chronic asthma with a daily inhaler.

def: The body's response to injury or infection, with redness, heat and swelling.
ex: Anti-inflammatory drugs reduced the inflammation in the joint.

def: The act of taking a patient into hospital for care.
ex: Her admission was arranged through the emergency department.

def: The close monitoring of a patient's condition over time.
ex: She was kept in overnight for observation.

def: The amount and frequency of a medicine to be taken.
ex: The doctor adjusted the dosage to control her symptoms.

def: A thin tube inserted into the body to drain fluid or give treatment.
ex: A catheter was fitted to drain the bladder.

def: Of a patient, to come in showing particular symptoms.
ex: The patient presented with fever and a persistent cough.
